content.content:
1	# Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm
2	
3	---
4	
5	## 1. Overview
6	
7	Zeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for all LLM execution: provider catalog,
8	route resolution, model selection, tool-call translation, execution
9	authorization, and MCP/UI/gRPC exposure. This spec governs absorbing
10	`crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's plugin/schema/D-Bus architecture and retiring
11	`op-llm` as an independent crate.
12	
13	**Primary authority file:**
14	`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`
15	
16	**D-Bus object:**
17	`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` on bus `org.opdbus.v1`
18	
19	**Schema re-export:**
20	`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`
21	
22	**Individual projection:**
23	`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`
24	
25	**Monolithic catalog:**
26	`/dev/shm/live-schema.json`
27	
28	**schemars is mandatory throughout this entire refactor.**
29	
30	Every struct that touches the Zeroclaw schema surface — `ZeroclawState`,
31	`LlmProjection`, `ModelRoute`, `Provider`, `SelectorPolicy`,
32	`SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`, `ZeroclawError`,
33	`GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` D-Bus property types, absorbed provider adapter
34	config structs — MUST derive `schemars::JsonSchema`. This is not optional.
35	The `PluginSchema` JSON is generated entirely from `schemars` output.
36	D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto field names, MCP tool parameter schemas, and
37	UI field renderers are all derived from the `schemars`-generated JSON Schema.
38	Any struct that does not carry `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` is
39	invisible to the system and cannot participate in the D-Bus/gRPC/MCP surface.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 2. Schema Field Changes
44	
45	### 2a. New fields on `ModelRoute`
46	(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`)
47	
48	```rust
49	pub cost_profile:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.cost-profile@v1
50	                                    // NOTE: exact field name/type confirmed by Schema Agent
51	                                    // spike against Zeroclaw's existing cost model schema.
52	                                    // Placeholder: cost_profile / budget_class / cost_policy.
53	pub effort_level:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.effort-level@v1
54	pub latency_class:     String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.latency-class@v1
55	pub privacy_tier:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1
56	pub context_window:    u32,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.context-window@v1
57	pub health_score:      f64,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1
58	pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1
59	pub tool_support:      Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1
60	```
61	
62	### 2b. New top-level field on `ZeroclawState`
63	(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`)
64	
65	```rust
66	pub selector_policy: SelectorPolicy,
67	// subid: sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1
68	```
69	
70	### 2c. New struct `SelectorPolicy`
71	(in `llm_projection.rs` or a new `selector.rs` under `common/`)
72	
73	```rust
74	pub struct SelectorPolicy {
75	    pub effort_weight:      f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.effort-weight@v1
76	    pub cost_weight:        f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.cost-weight@v1
77	                                  // coefficient applied to Zeroclaw's native cost field
78	    pub latency_weight:     f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.latency-weight@v1
79	    pub health_weight:      f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.health-weight@v1
80	    pub default_effort:     String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-effort@v1
81	    pub default_privacy_tier: String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-privacy@v1
82	}
83	```
84	
85	### 2d. New structs `SelectionInput` and `SelectionOutput`
86	
87	Exposed as D-Bus method shapes and MCP tool parameters. Defined in
88	`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`.
89	
90	`SelectionInput`:
91	```rust
92	pub task_class:         String,
93	pub requested_effort:   String,
94	pub cost_policy:        Option<String>,  // budget class or cost ceiling policy;
95	                                         // exact Zeroclaw field name confirmed by Schema Agent
96	pub latency_target:     Option<String>,
97	pub context_tokens:     u32,
98	pub privacy_tier:       String,
99	pub tool_needs:         Vec<String>,
100	pub explicit_provider:  Option<String>,
101	pub explicit_model:     Option<String>,
102	// subid: sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1
103	```
104	
105	`SelectionOutput`:
106	```rust
107	pub selected_provider:  String,
108	pub selected_model:     String,
109	pub reason:             String,
110	pub estimated_cost:     Option<String>,  // cost estimate in Zeroclaw's native units;
111	                                         // type/field confirmed by Schema Agent spike
112	pub effort_level:       String,
113	pub confidence:         f64,
114	pub fallback_routes:    Vec<String>,
115	pub event_metadata:     SelectionEvent,
116	// subid: sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1
117	```
118	
119	`SelectionEvent`:
120	```rust
121	pub trace_id:          String,
122	pub timestamp:         String,
123	pub selector_version:  String,
124	// subid: evt.service.zeroclaw.selection-event@v1
125	```
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 3. D-Bus Method/Property/Signal Shape
130	
131	See design.md §3 for the full table. Implementation notes:
132	
133	- `AuthorizeExecution` MUST check schema state atomically; it emits
134	  `ExecutionAuthorized` or `ExecutionDenied` signal.
135	- `SelectModel` runs the algorithm in design.md §4 using only
136	  `ZeroclawState` read from the D-Bus object's internal state; no env reads.
137	- All mutation methods (`SetProvider`, `SetModel`, `SelectModel`) MUST carry
138	  `actor_id` in the audit metadata and emit the corresponding signal.
139	- `ResolveRoute` is read-only (obs category); it does not mutate state.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 4. Dynamic Model Selection Implementation
144	
145	Location: new module
146	`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/selector.rs`
147	
148	Public entry point:
149	```rust
150	pub fn select_model(
151	    input: &SelectionInput,
152	    state: &ZeroclawState,
153	) -> Result<SelectionOutput, SelectionError>
154	```
155	
156	- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `state.projection.tools`.
157	- Reads `state.selector_policy` for weights.
158	- Implements Phase 1 hard filters and Phase 2 scoring as defined in
159	  design.md §4.
160	- Cost filter and scoring use Zeroclaw's native cost fields — the Schema Agent
161	  MUST confirm exact field names before implementation (placeholder:
162	  `cost_profile` / `budget_class`). No `cost_per_token` or incompatible
163	  unit math.
164	- Returns `SelectionError::RouteNotDeclared` if no candidate passes
165	  Phase 1.
166	- Pure function — no I/O, no env reads, deterministic given state.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 5. Layer Boundaries
171	
172	Two bad outcomes this spec explicitly prevents:
173	1. `op-llm` survives as a hidden authority under a new name.
174	2. `op-plugins` becomes a runtime blob mixing provider HTTP clients with schema authority.
175	
176	### Layer 1 — Zeroclaw Contract Layer
177	
178	Owns: `PluginSchema`, `ZeroclawState`, route declarations, provider catalog declarations, selector policy schema, OSCAL subids, generated D-Bus surface, `/dev/shm` schema projection spec.
179	
180	The Zeroclaw plugin IS its `PluginSchema`. The schema IS the plugin. `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for all calls.
181	
182	Must NOT contain: provider HTTP client implementations, network adapter code, wire-format parsing, or auth header construction.
183	
184	### Layer 2 — Zeroclaw Orchestration Layer
185	
186	Owns: dynamic model selection, effort/cost scoring, route resolution, execution authorization, fallback planning, `MutationEngine` integration, trace/event emission, handoff to provider adapters.
187	
188	Reads effective contract/state only through SchemaEngine / MutationEngine / D-Bus generated from `PluginSchema`. Does NOT implement provider wire formats directly.
189	
190	### Layer 3 — Provider Adapter Layer
191	
192	Owns: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenClaw / Factory / Kilocode / Opencode / OpenRouter / GCloudADC wire formats, request/response conversion, streaming parsing, auth headers, network calls.
193	
194	**Hard constraints:**
195	- Cannot select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass D-Bus, or execute undeclared schema routes.
196	- Takes only a schema-authorized execution plan from the Orchestration Layer.
197	- Must not call back into route selection or policy.
198	- Must not read `/dev/shm` paths or query D-Bus for live state.
199	- Provider adapters are replaceable implementation details under Zeroclaw authority.
200	
201	### Dependency Direction
202	
203	```
204	Contract Layer   → defines schema and generated D-Bus surface
205	Orchestration Layer  → consumes contract/state; produces execution plan
206	Provider Adapter Layer  → consumes execution plan; performs provider call
207	                          must not call back into Orchestration or Contract
208	```
209	
210	---
211	
212	## 6. Provider Adapter Absorption Plan
213	
214	### 5a. Source inventory
215	
216	Files to absorb from `crates/op-llm/src/`:
217	
218	| File | Contents |
219	|---|---|
220	| `provider.rs` | `LlmProvider` trait, `ChatMessage`, `ToolDefinition`, `ProviderType` |
221	| `chat.rs` | `ChatManager` — env-driven provider selection (to be replaced) |
222	| `anthropic.rs` | `AnthropicClient` |
223	| `gemini.rs` | `GeminiClient` |
224	| `gemini_cli.rs` | `create_gemini_cli_provider` |
225	| `factory.rs` | `FactoryProvider` |
226	| `openclaw.rs` | `OpenClawProvider` |
227	| `assistant.rs` | `AssistantProvider` |
228	| `gcloud_adc.rs` | `GCloudADCProvider` |
229	
230	### 5b. Absorption target
231	
232	The adapter code belongs inside the architecture boundary that holds Zeroclaw
233	execution logic — behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface, subordinate to Zeroclaw's
234	schema/D-Bus authority. Adapters MUST NOT become a second authority.
235	
236	The exact target module is identified by the Schema Agent and D-Bus Agent
237	as part of a short pre-implementation spike: inspect the
238	SchemaEngine/MutationEngine/gRPC-bridge dispatch boundary to name the existing
239	module before moving any code. The Provider Absorption Agent MUST record the
240	confirmed target in `handoff-provider-absorption.md` before moving files.
241	
242	Constraints:
243	- No new crate.
244	- `PluginSchema` authority (schema crate) must remain separate from adapter
245	  HTTP/runtime behavior. Do not put adapters inside `op-plugins` if doing so
246	  makes the schema crate own runtime I/O.
247	- Factory adapter is a provider category in Zeroclaw's catalog, not a
248	  separate D-Bus object.
249	
250	### 5c. `ChatManager` retirement
251	
252	`ChatManager`'s env-driven provider selection is replaced by the Zeroclaw
253	D-Bus `SelectModel` + `AuthorizeExecution` flow. `ChatManager` as a type is
254	removed from the public API after callers are migrated.
255	
256	### 5d. Compatibility shim
257	
258	During Caller Migration, a thin `pub use` re-export in `op-llm` preserves
259	the `LlmProvider` trait and `ChatMessage` type at their old paths for callers
260	not yet migrated. The shim is removed in the final Caller Migration task.
261	
262	---
263	
264	## 7. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract
265	
266	`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is a **derived `PluginSchema`
267	projection**, not a serialized live `ZeroclawState` file. The schema is the
268	plugin; the plugin is the schema.
269	
270	### Lifecycle
271	
272	`SchemaEngine` owns schema registration and projection. `MutationEngine` owns
273	validated state mutations against `PluginSchema`. The projection write is a
274	`SchemaEngine` concern, not an individual plugin's apply/mutate callback:
275	
276	1. `SchemaEngine` registers the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`.
277	2. On schema change or state update, `SchemaEngine` serializes the derived
278	   schema projection.
279	3. Writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json.tmp`.
280	4. `rename` `.tmp` → `zeroclaw.json` (atomic).
281	5. `SchemaEngine` aggregation pass writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`
282	   combining all plugin schemas. Individual plugins do NOT write it.
283	
284	### Read path
285	
286	- `op-grpc-bridge` and factory provider routes MAY read `zeroclaw.json` for
287	  discovery and display.
288	- `op-chat` and MCP MUST use D-Bus for execution-path decisions.
289	- No consumer writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.
290	
291	### Invariants
292	
293	- File does not exist → SchemaEngine has not registered Zeroclaw schema; callers must wait.
294	- File exists but stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; use D-Bus instead.
295	
296	---
297	
298	## 8. `op-llm` Retirement Stages
299	
300	| Stage | Action | Gate |
301	|---|---|---|
302	| 0 | Inventory all callers of `op-llm` | `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` baseline |
303	| 1 | Schema Agent extends `ZeroclawState` | `cargo check -p op-plugins` green |
304	| 2 | Provider Absorption Agent moves adapters | `cargo check -p op-llm` still green (compat shim) |
305	| 3 | Router Agent implements `select_model` | route-selection tests pass |
306	| 4 | Caller Migration Agent migrates `op-chat`, `op-web`, factory | `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` zero hits outside `op-llm` |
307	| 5 | Remove compat shim; remove `op-llm` from workspace | `cargo build --workspace` green without `op-llm` |
308	
309	---
310	
311	## 9. Multi-Agent Handoff Contract
312	
313	Each agent deposits a handoff file in `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/`.
314	Every handoff MUST contain these sections:
315	
316	```markdown
317	## Scope Completed
318	## Files Changed
319	## Contract Changes  (new types, trait changes, D-Bus signatures)
320	## Verification Commands Run
321	## Known Risks / Blocked Items
322	## Next-Agent Dependencies
323	```
324	
325	### Handoff files and responsible agents
326	
327	| File | Agent |
328	|---|---|
329	| `handoff-schema.md` | Schema Agent |
330	| `handoff-dbus.md` | D-Bus Agent |
331	| `handoff-provider-absorption.md` | Provider Absorption Agent |
332	| `handoff-router.md` | Router Agent |
333	| `handoff-callers.md` | Caller Migration Agent |
334	| `handoff-projection.md` | Projection Agent |
335	| `handoff-tests.md` | Test Agent |
336	| `handoff-review.md` | Review Agent |
337	
338	---
339	
340	## 10. Error Taxonomy
341	
342	```rust
343	pub enum ZeroclawError {
344	    RouteNotDeclared { hint: String },
345	    ProviderNotDeclared { provider: String },
346	    ModelNotDeclared { model: String },
347	    ToolNotDeclared { tool: String },
348	    RouteUnavailable { hint: String, reason: String },
349	    PrivacyTierViolation { required: String, provided: String },
350	    CostPolicyViolation { policy: String, reason: String },  // unit-neutral; exact fields confirmed by Schema Agent
351	    ContextWindowExceeded { limit: u32, requested: u32 },
352	    ExecutionDenied { reason: String },
353	    NoCandidateAfterFiltering,
354	}
355	// subid: sch.software.zeroclaw-error.schema@v1
356	```
357	
358	---
359	
360	## 12. D-Bus Projection ↔ gRPC-Bridge Integration
361	
362	The Zeroclaw projection tree MUST be wired through `op-grpc-bridge` so that
363	every Zeroclaw model route, provider catalog entry, and selection state is
364	published as a live D-Bus object tree consumable by `busctl` and `zbus`
365	clients. This is the primary call surface for Refactro and any other
366	schema-driven consumer. HTTP/env reads are prohibited for live execution state.
367	
368	### 12.1 Object tree
369	
370	The `SchemaEngine`/`op-grpc-bridge` projection step registers one managed
371	D-Bus object per logical Zeroclaw subject:
372	
373	| D-Bus path | Contents | busctl example |
374	|---|---|---|
375	| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` | `ZeroclawState` snapshot (top-level) | `busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw org.opdbus.v1 GetState` |
376	| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` | single `ModelRoute` | `busctl call ... GetRoute s "<hint>"` |
377	| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` | single `Provider` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` |
378	
379	`<hint>` is the `ModelRoute.hint` field (e.g. `kilocode-main`, `factory-fast`).
380	`<id>` is the `Provider.id` field.
381	
382	Sub-objects are registered by the `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` (§12.2) on every
383	schema projection cycle — not by `zeroclaw.rs` directly.
384	
385	### 12.2 GrpcBridgeProjectionHook
386	
387	New type in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_router.rs` (or a new
388	`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_projection.rs`):
389	
390	```rust
391	/// Reads the Zeroclaw PluginSchema projection from SchemaEngine and registers
392	/// each ModelRoute and Provider as a child D-Bus object under
393	/// /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/{routes,providers}/<id>.
394	pub struct GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
395	    connection: zbus::Connection,
396	    schema_engine: Arc<SchemaEngine>,
397	}
398	
399	impl GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
400	    /// Called by SchemaEngine after every zeroclaw schema projection cycle.
401	    /// Diffed against the previous cycle — only registers/removes changed objects.
402	    pub async fn apply_projection(&self, state: &ZeroclawState) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
403	}
404	```
405	
406	- Reads `ZeroclawState::projection.model_routes` and `.providers`.
407	- For each route: registers a D-Bus object at
408	  `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` implementing
409	  `org.opdbus.v1.ModelRoute` with the route's fields as D-Bus properties.
410	- For each provider: registers a D-Bus object at
411	  `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` implementing
412	  `org.opdbus.v1.Provider`.
413	- Objects removed from the projection are unregistered.
414	- D-Bus object data is derived **only** from the `PluginSchema` projection —
415	  never from env vars, `/dev/shm` direct reads, or any source other than
416	  `SchemaEngine`.
417	
418	### 12.3 Calling Zeroclaw from Refactro (busctl / zbus)
419	
420	**Read model routes (busctl):**
421	```bash
422	# List all routes
423	busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
424	  org.opdbus.v1 GetModelRoutes
425	
426	# Introspect a specific route object
427	busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 \
428	  /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/kilocode-main
429	```
430	
431	**Select a model (busctl):**
432	```bash
433	busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
434	  org.opdbus.v1 SelectModel \
435	  s '{"task_class":"code","requested_effort":"high","context_tokens":4096,"privacy_tier":"internal","tool_needs":[]}'
436	```
437	
438	**Authorize execution (busctl):**
439	```bash
440	busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
441	  org.opdbus.v1 AuthorizeExecution \
442	  sss "factory" "kilocode-main" ""
443	```
444	
445	**Read route via zbus (Rust):**
446	```rust
447	use zbus::proxy;
448	
449	#[proxy(
450	    interface = "org.opdbus.v1.ModelRoute",
451	    default_service = "org.opdbus.v1",
452	    default_path = "/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/kilocode-main"
453	)]
454	trait ModelRoute {
455	    #[zbus(property)]
456	    fn model(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
457	    #[zbus(property)]
458	    fn available(&self) -> zbus::Result<bool>;
459	    #[zbus(property)]
460	    fn effort_level(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
461	    #[zbus(property)]
462	    fn privacy_tier(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
463	}
464	```
465	
466	### 12.4 gRPC streaming of Zeroclaw state
467	
468	`op-grpc-bridge`'s `SchemaPassthroughService` (already present in
469	`schema_passthrough.rs`) MUST serve Zeroclaw's schema projection over the
470	`operation.v1.PluginService` gRPC stream so remote consumers (e.g.
471	`cognitive-mcp` on WireGuard) can subscribe to route/provider changes
472	without polling D-Bus directly.
473	
474	The projection snapshot published per stream message contains:
475	- `plugin_name: "zeroclaw"`
476	- `schema_json: <ZeroclawState as PluginSchema serialized>`
477	- `model_routes: <repeated ModelRoute protos>`
478	- `providers: <repeated Provider protos>`
479	
480	Proto shape additions belong in `operation.proto` under a new
481	`ZeroclawProjection` message. `SchemaRouter` routes the `zeroclaw` plugin name
482	to this projection.
483	
484	### 12.5 OSCAL subids for grpc-bridge projection
485	
486	| subid | category | subject |
487	|---|---|---|
488	| `prj.service.zeroclaw-bridge.route-objects@v1` | prj | GrpcBridgeProjectionHook registers route sub-objects |
489	| `prj.service.zeroclaw-bridge.provider-objects@v1` | prj | GrpcBridgeProjectionHook registers provider sub-objects |
490	| `exp.service.zeroclaw-bridge.grpc-stream@v1` | exp | SchemaPassthroughService streams ZeroclawProjection |
491	| `obs.service.zeroclaw-bridge.route-property@v1` | obs | D-Bus property read on a route sub-object |
492	| `obs.service.zeroclaw-bridge.provider-property@v1` | obs | D-Bus property read on a provider sub-object |
493	
494	### 12.6 Non-goals for this integration
495	
496	- Refactro MUST NOT call `op-llm` HTTP endpoints directly.
497	- Refactro MUST NOT read `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` as its
498	  primary live state. It uses D-Bus (§12.3) or the gRPC stream (§12.4).
499	- The grpc-bridge does NOT own model selection logic — it only projects what
500	  `SchemaEngine` has registered. Selection calls flow through D-Bus
501	  `SelectModel` / `AuthorizeExecution` methods on the top-level plugin object.
502	
503	---
504	
505	## 11. OSCAL Subid Registry (new subids introduced by this spec)
506	
507	| subid | category | subject |
508	|---|---|---|
509	| `sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1` | sch | SelectorPolicy struct |
510	| `sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1` | sch | SelectionInput struct |
511	| `sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1` | sch | SelectionOutput struct |
512	| `evt.service.zeroclaw.selection-event@v1` | evt | SelectionEvent struct |
513	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.cost-profile@v1` | obs | ModelRoute cost field (placeholder; exact name confirmed by Schema Agent) |
514	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.effort-level@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.effort_level |
515	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.latency-class@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.latency_class |
516	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.privacy_tier |
517	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.context-window@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.context_window |
518	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.health_score |
519	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.fallback_routes |
520	| `obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.tool_support |
521	| `mut.service.zeroclaw.select-model@v1` | mut | D-Bus SelectModel method |
522	| `mut.service.zeroclaw.authorize-execution@v1` | mut | D-Bus AuthorizeExecution method |
523	| `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-provider@v1` | mut | D-Bus SetProvider method |
524	| `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-model@v1` | mut | D-Bus SetModel method |
525	| `obs.service.zeroclaw.resolve-route@v1` | obs | D-Bus ResolveRoute method |
526	| `obs.service.zeroclaw.provider-catalog@v1` | obs | D-Bus GetProviderCatalog method |
527	| `obs.service.zeroclaw.model-routes@v1` | obs | D-Bus GetModelRoutes method |
528	| `obs.service.zeroclaw.tools@v1` | obs | D-Bus GetTools method |
529	| `prj.service.zeroclaw.schema-json@v1` | prj | D-Bus SchemaJson property |
530	| `evt.service.zeroclaw.provider-changed@v1` | evt | ProviderChanged signal |
531	| `evt.service.zeroclaw.model-changed@v1` | evt | ModelChanged signal |

# Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm

---

## 1. Overview

Zeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for all LLM execution: provider catalog,
route resolution, model selection, tool-call translation, execution
authorization, and MCP/UI/gRPC exposure. This spec governs absorbing
`crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's plugin/schema/D-Bus architecture and retiring
`op-llm` as an independent crate.

**Primary authority file:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`

**D-Bus object:**
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` on bus `org.opdbus.v1`

**Schema re-export:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`

**Individual projection:**
`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`

**Monolithic catalog:**
`/dev/shm/live-schema.json`

**schemars is mandatory throughout this entire refactor.**

Every struct that touches the Zeroclaw schema surface — `ZeroclawState`,
`LlmProjection`, `ModelRoute`, `Provider`, `SelectorPolicy`,
`SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`, `ZeroclawError`,
`GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` D-Bus property types, absorbed provider adapter
config structs — MUST derive `schemars::JsonSchema`. This is not optional.
The `PluginSchema` JSON is generated entirely from `schemars` output.
D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto field names, MCP tool parameter schemas, and
UI field renderers are all derived from the `schemars`-generated JSON Schema.
Any struct that does not carry `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` is
invisible to the system and cannot participate in the D-Bus/gRPC/MCP surface.

---

## 2. Schema Field Changes

### 2a. New fields on `ModelRoute`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`)

```rust
pub cost_profile:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.cost-profile@v1
                                    // NOTE: exact field name/type confirmed by Schema Agent
                                    // spike against Zeroclaw's existing cost model schema.
                                    // Placeholder: cost_profile / budget_class / cost_policy.
pub effort_level:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.effort-level@v1
pub latency_class:     String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.latency-class@v1
pub privacy_tier:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1
pub context_window:    u32,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.context-window@v1
pub health_score:      f64,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1
pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1
pub tool_support:      Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1
```

### 2b. New top-level field on `ZeroclawState`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`)

```rust
pub selector_policy: SelectorPolicy,
// subid: sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1
```

### 2c. New struct `SelectorPolicy`
(in `llm_projection.rs` or a new `selector.rs` under `common/`)

```rust
pub struct SelectorPolicy {
    pub effort_weight:      f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.effort-weight@v1
    pub cost_weight:        f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.cost-weight@v1
                                  // coefficient applied to Zeroclaw's native cost field
    pub latency_weight:     f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.latency-weight@v1
    pub health_weight:      f64,  // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.health-weight@v1
    pub default_effort:     String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-effort@v1
    pub default_privacy_tier: String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-privacy@v1
}
```

### 2d. New structs `SelectionInput` and `SelectionOutput`

Exposed as D-Bus method shapes and MCP tool parameters. Defined in
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`.

`SelectionInput`:
```rust
pub task_class:         String,
pub requested_effort:   String,
pub cost_policy:        Option<String>,  // budget class or cost ceiling policy;
                                         // exact Zeroclaw field name confirmed by Schema Agent
pub latency_target:     Option<String>,
pub context_tokens:     u32,
pub privacy_tier:       String,
pub tool_needs:         Vec<String>,
pub explicit_provider:  Option<String>,
pub explicit_model:     Option<String>,
// subid: sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1
```

`SelectionOutput`:
```rust
pub selected_provider:  String,
pub selected_model:     String,
pub reason:             String,
pub estimated_cost:     Option<String>,  // cost estimate in Zeroclaw's native units;
                                         // type/field confirmed by Schema Agent spike
pub effort_level:       String,
pub confidence:         f64,
pub fallback_routes:    Vec<String>,
pub event_metadata:     SelectionEvent,
// subid: sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1
```

`SelectionEvent`:
```rust
pub trace_id:          String,
pub timestamp:         String,
pub selector_version:  String,
// subid: evt.service.zeroclaw.selection-event@v1
```

---

## 3. D-Bus Method/Property/Signal Shape

See design.md §3 for the full table. Implementation notes:

- `AuthorizeExecution` MUST check schema state atomically; it emits
  `ExecutionAuthorized` or `ExecutionDenied` signal.
- `SelectModel` runs the algorithm in design.md §4 using only
  `ZeroclawState` read from the D-Bus object's internal state; no env reads.
- All mutation methods (`SetProvider`, `SetModel`, `SelectModel`) MUST carry
  `actor_id` in the audit metadata and emit the corresponding signal.
- `ResolveRoute` is read-only (obs category); it does not mutate state.

---

## 4. Dynamic Model Selection Implementation

Location: new module
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/selector.rs`

Public entry point:
```rust
pub fn select_model(
    input: &SelectionInput,
    state: &ZeroclawState,
) -> Result<SelectionOutput, SelectionError>
```

- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `state.projection.tools`.
- Reads `state.selector_policy` for weights.
- Implements Phase 1 hard filters and Phase 2 scoring as defined in
  design.md §4.
- Cost filter and scoring use Zeroclaw's native cost fields — the Schema Agent
  MUST confirm exact field names before implementation (placeholder:
  `cost_profile` / `budget_class`). No `cost_per_token` or incompatible
  unit math.
- Returns `SelectionError::RouteNotDeclared` if no candidate passes
  Phase 1.
- Pure function — no I/O, no env reads, deterministic given state.

---

## 5. Layer Boundaries

Two bad outcomes this spec explicitly prevents:
1. `op-llm` survives as a hidden authority under a new name.
2. `op-plugins` becomes a runtime blob mixing provider HTTP clients with schema authority.

### Layer 1 — Zeroclaw Contract Layer

Owns: `PluginSchema`, `ZeroclawState`, route declarations, provider catalog declarations, selector policy schema, OSCAL subids, generated D-Bus surface, `/dev/shm` schema projection spec.

The Zeroclaw plugin IS its `PluginSchema`. The schema IS the plugin. `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for all calls.

Must NOT contain: provider HTTP client implementations, network adapter code, wire-format parsing, or auth header construction.

### Layer 2 — Zeroclaw Orchestration Layer

Owns: dynamic model selection, effort/cost scoring, route resolution, execution authorization, fallback planning, `MutationEngine` integration, trace/event emission, handoff to provider adapters.

Reads effective contract/state only through SchemaEngine / MutationEngine / D-Bus generated from `PluginSchema`. Does NOT implement provider wire formats directly.

### Layer 3 — Provider Adapter Layer

Owns: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenClaw / Factory / Kilocode / Opencode / OpenRouter / GCloudADC wire formats, request/response conversion, streaming parsing, auth headers, network calls.

**Hard constraints:**
- Cannot select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass D-Bus, or execute undeclared schema routes.
- Takes only a schema-authorized execution plan from the Orchestration Layer.
- Must not call back into route selection or policy.
- Must not read `/dev/shm` paths or query D-Bus for live state.
- Provider adapters are replaceable implementation details under Zeroclaw authority.

### Dependency Direction

```
Contract Layer   → defines schema and generated D-Bus surface
Orchestration Layer  → consumes contract/state; produces execution plan
Provider Adapter Layer  → consumes execution plan; performs provider call
                          must not call back into Orchestration or Contract
```

---

## 6. Provider Adapter Absorption Plan

### 5a. Source inventory

Files to absorb from `crates/op-llm/src/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `provider.rs` | `LlmProvider` trait, `ChatMessage`, `ToolDefinition`, `ProviderType` |
| `chat.rs` | `ChatManager` — env-driven provider selection (to be replaced) |
| `anthropic.rs` | `AnthropicClient` |
| `gemini.rs` | `GeminiClient` |
| `gemini_cli.rs` | `create_gemini_cli_provider` |
| `factory.rs` | `FactoryProvider` |
| `openclaw.rs` | `OpenClawProvider` |
| `assistant.rs` | `AssistantProvider` |
| `gcloud_adc.rs` | `GCloudADCProvider` |

### 5b. Absorption target

The adapter code belongs inside the architecture boundary that holds Zeroclaw
execution logic — behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface, subordinate to Zeroclaw's
schema/D-Bus authority. Adapters MUST NOT become a second authority.

The exact target module is identified by the Schema Agent and D-Bus Agent
as part of a short pre-implementation spike: inspect the
SchemaEngine/MutationEngine/gRPC-bridge dispatch boundary to name the existing
module before moving any code. The Provider Absorption Agent MUST record the
confirmed target in `handoff-provider-absorption.md` before moving files.

Constraints:
- No new crate.
- `PluginSchema` authority (schema crate) must remain separate from adapter
  HTTP/runtime behavior. Do not put adapters inside `op-plugins` if doing so
  makes the schema crate own runtime I/O.
- Factory adapter is a provider category in Zeroclaw's catalog, not a
  separate D-Bus object.

### 5c. `ChatManager` retirement

`ChatManager`'s env-driven provider selection is replaced by the Zeroclaw
D-Bus `SelectModel` + `AuthorizeExecution` flow. `ChatManager` as a type is
removed from the public API after callers are migrated.

### 5d. Compatibility shim

During Caller Migration, a thin `pub use` re-export in `op-llm` preserves
the `LlmProvider` trait and `ChatMessage` type at their old paths for callers
not yet migrated. The shim is removed in the final Caller Migration task.

---

## 7. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract

`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is a **derived `PluginSchema`
projection**, not a serialized live `ZeroclawState` file. The schema is the
plugin; the plugin is the schema.

### Lifecycle

`SchemaEngine` owns schema registration and projection. `MutationEngine` owns
validated state mutations against `PluginSchema`. The projection write is a
`SchemaEngine` concern, not an individual plugin's apply/mutate callback:

1. `SchemaEngine` registers the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`.
2. On schema change or state update, `SchemaEngine` serializes the derived
   schema projection.
3. Writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json.tmp`.
4. `rename` `.tmp` → `zeroclaw.json` (atomic).
5. `SchemaEngine` aggregation pass writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`
   combining all plugin schemas. Individual plugins do NOT write it.

### Read path

- `op-grpc-bridge` and factory provider routes MAY read `zeroclaw.json` for
  discovery and display.
- `op-chat` and MCP MUST use D-Bus for execution-path decisions.
- No consumer writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.

### Invariants

- File does not exist → SchemaEngine has not registered Zeroclaw schema; callers must wait.
- File exists but stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; use D-Bus instead.

---

## 8. `op-llm` Retirement Stages

| Stage | Action | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Inventory all callers of `op-llm` | `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` baseline |
| 1 | Schema Agent extends `ZeroclawState` | `cargo check -p op-plugins` green |
| 2 | Provider Absorption Agent moves adapters | `cargo check -p op-llm` still green (compat shim) |
| 3 | Router Agent implements `select_model` | route-selection tests pass |
| 4 | Caller Migration Agent migrates `op-chat`, `op-web`, factory | `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` zero hits outside `op-llm` |
| 5 | Remove compat shim; remove `op-llm` from workspace | `cargo build --workspace` green without `op-llm` |

---

## 9. Multi-Agent Handoff Contract

Each agent deposits a handoff file in `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/`.
Every handoff MUST contain these sections:

```markdown
## Scope Completed
## Files Changed
## Contract Changes  (new types, trait changes, D-Bus signatures)
## Verification Commands Run
## Known Risks / Blocked Items
## Next-Agent Dependencies
```

### Handoff files and responsible agents

| File | Agent |
|---|---|
| `handoff-schema.md` | Schema Agent |
| `handoff-dbus.md` | D-Bus Agent |
| `handoff-provider-absorption.md` | Provider Absorption Agent |
| `handoff-router.md` | Router Agent |
| `handoff-callers.md` | Caller Migration Agent |
| `handoff-projection.md` | Projection Agent |
| `handoff-tests.md` | Test Agent |
| `handoff-review.md` | Review Agent |

---

## 10. Error Taxonomy

```rust
pub enum ZeroclawError {
    RouteNotDeclared { hint: String },
    ProviderNotDeclared { provider: String },
    ModelNotDeclared { model: String },
    ToolNotDeclared { tool: String },
    RouteUnavailable { hint: String, reason: String },
    PrivacyTierViolation { required: String, provided: String },
    CostPolicyViolation { policy: String, reason: String },  // unit-neutral; exact fields confirmed by Schema Agent
    ContextWindowExceeded { limit: u32, requested: u32 },
    ExecutionDenied { reason: String },
    NoCandidateAfterFiltering,
}
// subid: sch.software.zeroclaw-error.schema@v1
```

---

## 12. D-Bus Projection ↔ gRPC-Bridge Integration

The Zeroclaw projection tree MUST be wired through `op-grpc-bridge` so that
every Zeroclaw model route, provider catalog entry, and selection state is
published as a live D-Bus object tree consumable by `busctl` and `zbus`
clients. This is the primary call surface for Refactro and any other
schema-driven consumer. HTTP/env reads are prohibited for live execution state.

### 12.1 Object tree

The `SchemaEngine`/`op-grpc-bridge` projection step registers one managed
D-Bus object per logical Zeroclaw subject:

| D-Bus path | Contents | busctl example |
|---|---|---|
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` | `ZeroclawState` snapshot (top-level) | `busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw org.opdbus.v1 GetState` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` | single `ModelRoute` | `busctl call ... GetRoute s "<hint>"` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` | single `Provider` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` |

`<hint>` is the `ModelRoute.hint` field (e.g. `kilocode-main`, `factory-fast`).
`<id>` is the `Provider.id` field.

Sub-objects are registered by the `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` (§12.2) on every
schema projection cycle — not by `zeroclaw.rs` directly.

### 12.2 GrpcBridgeProjectionHook

New type in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_router.rs` (or a new
`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_projection.rs`):

```rust
/// Reads the Zeroclaw PluginSchema projection from SchemaEngine and registers
/// each ModelRoute and Provider as a child D-Bus object under
/// /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/{routes,providers}/<id>.
pub struct GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    connection: zbus::Connection,
    schema_engine: Arc<SchemaEngine>,
}

impl GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    /// Called by SchemaEngine after every zeroclaw schema projection cycle.
    /// Diffed against the previous cycle — only registers/removes changed objects.
    pub async fn apply_projection(&self, state: &ZeroclawState) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
}
```

- Reads `ZeroclawState::projection.model_routes` and `.providers`.
- For each route: registers a D-Bus object at
  `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` implementing
  `org.opdbus.v1.ModelRoute` with the route's fields as D-Bus properties.
- For each provider: registers a D-Bus object at
  `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` implementing
  `org.opdbus.v1.Provider`.
- Objects removed from the projection are unregistered.
- D-Bus object data is derived **only** from the `PluginSchema` projection —
  never from env vars, `/dev/shm` direct reads, or any source other than
  `SchemaEngine`.

### 12.3 Calling Zeroclaw from Refactro (busctl / zbus)

**Read model routes (busctl):**
```bash
# List all routes
busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
  org.opdbus.v1 GetModelRoutes

# Introspect a specific route object
busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 \
  /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/kilocode-main
```

**Select a model (busctl):**
```bash
busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
  org.opdbus.v1 SelectModel \
  s '{"task_class":"code","requested_effort":"high","context_tokens":4096,"privacy_tier":"internal","tool_needs":[]}'
```

**Authorize execution (busctl):**
```bash
busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw \
  org.opdbus.v1 AuthorizeExecution \
  sss "factory" "kilocode-main" ""
```

**Read route via zbus (Rust):**
```rust
use zbus::proxy;

#[proxy(
    interface = "org.opdbus.v1.ModelRoute",
    default_service = "org.opdbus.v1",
    default_path = "/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/kilocode-main"
)]
trait ModelRoute {
    #[zbus(property)]
    fn model(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
    #[zbus(property)]
    fn available(&self) -> zbus::Result<bool>;
    #[zbus(property)]
    fn effort_level(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
    #[zbus(property)]
    fn privacy_tier(&self) -> zbus::Result<String>;
}
```

### 12.4 gRPC streaming of Zeroclaw state

`op-grpc-bridge`'s `SchemaPassthroughService` (already present in
`schema_passthrough.rs`) MUST serve Zeroclaw's schema projection over the
`operation.v1.PluginService` gRPC stream so remote consumers (e.g.
`cognitive-mcp` on WireGuard) can subscribe to route/provider changes
without polling D-Bus directly.

The projection snapshot published per stream message contains:
- `plugin_name: "zeroclaw"`
- `schema_json: <ZeroclawState as PluginSchema serialized>`
- `model_routes: <repeated ModelRoute protos>`
- `providers: <repeated Provider protos>`

Proto shape additions belong in `operation.proto` under a new
`ZeroclawProjection` message. `SchemaRouter` routes the `zeroclaw` plugin name
to this projection.

### 12.5 OSCAL subids for grpc-bridge projection

| subid | category | subject |
|---|---|---|
| `prj.service.zeroclaw-bridge.route-objects@v1` | prj | GrpcBridgeProjectionHook registers route sub-objects |
| `prj.service.zeroclaw-bridge.provider-objects@v1` | prj | GrpcBridgeProjectionHook registers provider sub-objects |
| `exp.service.zeroclaw-bridge.grpc-stream@v1` | exp | SchemaPassthroughService streams ZeroclawProjection |
| `obs.service.zeroclaw-bridge.route-property@v1` | obs | D-Bus property read on a route sub-object |
| `obs.service.zeroclaw-bridge.provider-property@v1` | obs | D-Bus property read on a provider sub-object |

### 12.6 Non-goals for this integration

- Refactro MUST NOT call `op-llm` HTTP endpoints directly.
- Refactro MUST NOT read `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` as its
  primary live state. It uses D-Bus (§12.3) or the gRPC stream (§12.4).
- The grpc-bridge does NOT own model selection logic — it only projects what
  `SchemaEngine` has registered. Selection calls flow through D-Bus
  `SelectModel` / `AuthorizeExecution` methods on the top-level plugin object.

---

| subid | category | subject |
|---|---|---|
| `sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1` | sch | SelectorPolicy struct |
| `sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1` | sch | SelectionInput struct |
| `sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1` | sch | SelectionOutput struct |

| `obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.privacy_tier |

| `obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.health_score |
| `obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.fallback_routes |
| `obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1` | obs | ModelRoute.tool_support |
| `mut.service.zeroclaw.select-model@v1` | mut | D-Bus SelectModel method |

# Tasks — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm

Execution model: **orchestrated multi-agent**. The Coordinator Agent sequences
agent phases, manages the integration branch, and owns the final acceptance
gate. Agents work concurrently within a phase only when their inputs do not
depend on each other. All agents deposit handoff files per spec.md §8 before
the next phase proceeds.

---

## Phase 0 — Baseline (Coordinator Agent)

### T-00: Inventory `op-llm` consumers and establish baseline

**Agent:** Coordinator
**Inputs:** None
**Actions:**
1. Run `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` across workspace; record all consumer
   files and import paths. Also run `rg 'op-llm' crates -g Cargo.toml` to
   find all crate dependencies.
2. Run `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`
   baseline; record pass/fail counts.
3. Verify `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` write path is active (via
   SchemaEngine projection) in current state.
4. Commit baseline with a `[baseline]` tag.

**Verification:**
```bash
rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs' -l
rg 'op-llm' crates -g 'Cargo.toml'
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features 2>&1 | tail -20
```

**Gate:** Baseline test counts recorded; consumer list in handoff.

---

## Phase 1 — Schema Extension (Schema Agent)

### T-10: Extend `ModelRoute` with selector fields

**Agent:** Schema
**File:** `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`
**Actions:**
1. **Pre-implementation spike:** Inspect Zeroclaw's existing cost model/config
   schema to identify the correct cost field name(s) and type(s). Record
   findings in `handoff-schema.md` before naming any field.
2. Add fields to `ModelRoute`: `cost_profile` (or confirmed Zeroclaw-native
   name), `effort_level`, `latency_class`, `privacy_tier`, `context_window`,
   `health_score`, `fallback_routes`, `tool_support`.
3. `ModelRoute` MUST carry `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]`.
   Every new field MUST also be visible to `schemars` — no `#[serde(skip)]`
   on schema-contract fields, no manual `impl JsonSchema`.
4. Annotate each field with `x-oscal-subid` per spec.md §11 (update the
   `cost_profile` subid entry once the real name is confirmed).
5. Add `serde(default)` on all new fields.

**Verification:**
```bash
cargo check -p op-plugins
cargo test -p op-plugins -- zeroclaw_schema_golden
```

### T-11: Add `SelectorPolicy` struct and `SelectionInput`/`SelectionOutput`

**Agent:** Schema
**Files:**
- `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`
  (add `SelectorPolicy`, `SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`)
- `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`
  (add `selector_policy: SelectorPolicy` to `ZeroclawState`)
**Actions:**
1. Define all four structs with `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]`.
   `schemars::JsonSchema` is mandatory — without it these types are invisible
   to D-Bus method shape generation, MCP tool parameters, and gRPC proto fields.
2. Annotate structs and fields with OSCAL subids from spec.md §11.
3. Add `selector_policy` field to `ZeroclawState`.
4. Update `zeroclaw_schema_golden()` to include `selector_policy` defaults.
5. Confirm `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` contains `selector_policy`,
   `selection_input`, and `selection_output` definitions in output.

**Verification:**
```bash
cargo check -p op-plugins
cargo test -p op-plugins -- zeroclaw
```

### T-12: Add `ZeroclawError` enum

**Agent:** Schema
**File:** `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs` (or a new
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/errors.rs`)
**Actions:**
1. Define `ZeroclawError` with all variants from spec.md §10.
2. Derive `thiserror::Error` AND `schemars::JsonSchema` — the error schema
   is surfaced in MCP tool responses and D-Bus method error payloads.
3. Annotate with `sch.software.zeroclaw-error.schema@v1`.

**Verification:**
```bash
cargo check -p op-plugins
```

### T-13: Update `plugin_schema_defs.rs` re-export and golden test

**Agent:** Schema
**File:** `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`
**Actions:**
1. Ensure new types are accessible via the re-export path.
2. Update the golden schema snapshot test if one exists; add one if not.
3. Run subid uniqueness check (grep for duplicate `x-oscal-subid` values).

**Verification:**

Grounded the check against the actual code. Short answer: **mostly, but not all — it nails the two things you flagged and leaves ~4 reconciliation gaps.**

## What the rewrite *does* address
- **schemars mandate** — §1 makes it global and every Phase-1 task now requires `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`. Solid.
- **grpc-bridge owns the D-Bus objects** — new §12 + Phase 1b (T-15–T-18): `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` materializes one D-Bus object per route/provider, **derived only from the single SchemaEngine `PluginSchema` projection**. That's the single-source model you asked for, and it's the call surface for busctl/zbus/Refactro.

## Gaps it does *not* resolve

1. **It didn't remove the second projection — it added a representation on top of it.** §7 still mandates the `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` file projection, and §12 adds the D-Bus object tree, and §12.4 adds a third `ZeroclawProjection` gRPC proto. They all derive from one source (good), but T-16 has the bridge hook *read the just-written `/dev/shm` JSON* to build the D-Bus objects — so the file is still the intermediate. If "no second projection" meant *the D-Bus tree replaces the `/dev/shm` file*, that's not done; if it meant *one source of authority, many views*, it's fine. **This is the one real decision to settle.**

2. **Circular-dependency risk, unaddressed.** §12.2 puts `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` (holding `Arc<SchemaEngine>`) in `op-grpc-bridge`, and says SchemaEngine calls it each cycle. But the projection authority — `SchemaEngine` — actually lives in **`op-projection`**, not `op-grpc-bridge` or `op-plugins`. "SchemaEngine calls a hook in op-grpc-bridge" implies `op-projection → op-grpc-bridge → op-projection`. The spec never resolves who depends on whom.

3. **"PluginSchema generated entirely from schemars" (§1) isn't reconciled with reality.** Today `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` builds the `PluginSchema` via `schema_from_state()` (introspecting the serialized JSON) + hand-written method/signal decls. Nothing calls `schemars::schema_for!`. The spec asserts the schemars output *is* the PluginSchema but never says how to bridge schemars → the existing `PluginSchemaBuilder`/`FieldSchema` model.

4. **`x-oscal-subid` annotation mechanism is undefined.** The T-13/T-80 checklist greps source for `x-oscal-subid`, but the codebase's subid convention is the `PluginSchema.subids: HashMap` map, and schemars 0.8 can't cleanly emit field-level extension keys. Two incompatible mechanisms, unreconciled. (Minor siblings: T-15 hardcodes D-Bus property names while §12 says "derive from schemars"; `zeroclaw.rs` transport uses `/opdbus/v1/...` while the canonical servers + spec use `/org/opdbus/v1/...`.)

## Where I am
Mid Phase-1: added `schemars` to the workspace + `op-plugins`, and wrote the typed `common/llm_projection.rs` (all structs derive `JsonSchema`). I have **not** yet wired `pub mod common`, converted `zeroclaw.rs`, or touched `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` — so nothing is half-broken.

=== FACTORY-MISSION head ===
# Factory Mission: Implement the Plugin Capability Source-of-Truth Spec (TDD-orchestrated)

## Mission
Implement the spec at `.kiro/specs/plugin-capability-source-of-truth/`
(`requirements.md` = 13 requirements + 5 NFRs, `design.md`, `tasks.md` = 57
tasks). This consolidates the plugin pipeline so that **the plugin is the sole
source of truth for every object's existence**, defines a **capability as the
complete enumerable method/function/property/signal surface of an object**, and
makes the gRPC bridge the single owner/registrar/projected-tree fed by
`Producer → SHM → Bridge`.

`tasks.md` is the authoritative work breakdown and is already ordered so the
workspace builds at each step. Every task carries `_Requirements: X.Y_` — honor
that traceability.

## Method: TDD-orchestrated
Use the enabled skills: `tdd-orchestrator`, `test-automator`,
`spec-to-code-compliance`, `rust-pro`, `rust-async-patterns`,
`systems-programming-rust-project`, `orchestrate-batch-refactor`.

For each requirement group:
1. **RED** — write tests directly from that requirement's EARS acceptance
   criteria (WHEN/WHILE/IF/WHERE … SHALL …). One test per criterion where
   feasible. Tests must fail first.
2. **GREEN** — implement the minimum to pass.
3. **REFACTOR** — clean up; keep the workspace compiling.
4. **VERIFY** — `spec-to-code-compliance`: confirm every acceptance criterion in
   the group is satisfied before moving on.

## Orchestration (workstreams)
Decompose `tasks.md` into these dependency-ordered workstreams; parallelize
within a workstream, gate between them on a green build:

- **WS1 — Capability model & dedup** (R1, R2): plugin trait declares the full
  capability surface (methods/functions w/ arg+return schema, side-effect class,
  required-capability, properties, signals, guarantees); collapse the duplicate
  `PluginCapabilities` (op-state vs op-plugins) to one.
- **WS2 — Producer → SHM** (R3, R9, R10, R11): op-projection emits the complete
  capability schema + present-state into SHM (per-plugin files + monolith +
  atomic manifest with the single catalog_hash); subid taxonomy on every
  capability; serialization completeness.
- **WS3 — Bridge as sole owner/registrar/projected-tree** (R4, R5, R6): bridge
  owns the plugins bus name, registers the tree from SHM, real dispatch through
  `SchemaEngine.mutate` (NO stub, `json_args` used), method validation against
  the schema capability surface.
- **WS4 — Capability enforcement** (R7): enforce `capability_id` against the
  caller identity (footprint/sessionid from GhostbridgeInterceptor) at the
  bridge — the single enforcement point.
- **WS5 — Trim redundant registrars & dead claims** (R8): op-dbus-mirror drops
  plugin-object registration + its `org.opdbus.v1` name claim (keeps ovsdb/
  nonnet/mirror-mgmt); op-projection drops D-Bus object serving (producer-only);
  delete the dead op-state name claim, op-openvswitch bare-name claim, and the
  orphan `opdbus` service/binary.
- **WS6 — Autogeneration + Gemma** (R12, R13): the missing-plugin lifecycle
  (research → synthesize full capability surface → review → persist as the plugin
  → project → serve; with quarantine until approved), and route object-property/
  capability research through **Gemma** (replace the
  `create_agent("search-specialist")` seam in
  `auto_create.rs::query_elements_via_agent`). Gemma is a plugin/StatePlugin.

## Hard rules (do not violate — these are why prior attempts failed)
- **NO stubs, NO placeholders, NO "for now"/"in a full implementation" comments.**
  A registered object that returns fake success or validates against an empty set
  is a defect. The recurring failure mode here is inert code that *looks* wired.
- **One schema, one source, computed in exactly ONE place.** Never recompute the
  catalog_hash in a consumer; consumers read the manifest hash.
- **Only valid path is `org.opdbus.v1.plugins`.** No new
  `operation.<domain>.v1.*Service` protos; no raw ip:port.
- **SHM is authoritative present-state; READ it. NO polling loops, NO watchers.**

# Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm

---

## 1. Overview

Zeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for all LLM execution: provider catalog,
route resolution, model selection, tool-call translation, execution
authorization, and MCP/UI/gRPC exposure. This spec governs absorbing
`crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's plugin/schema/D-Bus architecture and retiring
`op-llm` as an independent crate.

**Primary authority file:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`

**Schema types (contract layer):**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`

**Schema re-export / `PluginSchema` builder:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`

**Single projection authority (producer):**
`crates/op-projection` → `SchemaEngine`

**D-Bus object tree (view, generated by the bridge):**
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` and children, on bus `org.opdbus.v1`

### 1.1 One projection — non-negotiable

There is **exactly one** projection of Zeroclaw, and it is owned by
`op-projection::SchemaEngine`. The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` (derived from
`ZeroclawState`) is the single source of truth. Everything else is a **view**
derived from that one schema, never a second computation:

- The **D-Bus object tree** under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/...` is a
  live view materialized by `op-grpc-bridge` directly from the in-memory
  `PluginSchema` held by `SchemaEngine` (§9). This is the primary call surface.
- The **`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`** file is a **non-authoritative
  discovery snapshot** written by `SchemaEngine` for human/tooling inspection.
  It is **never read back** to build the D-Bus tree, and **never** used for
  execution-path decisions (§7).
- The **gRPC stream** (`ZeroclawProjection`) is a serialized view of the same
  `PluginSchema`, for remote subscribers (§9.4).

No component computes, mutates, or re-derives the projection except
`SchemaEngine`. The bridge, the file, and the gRPC stream are read-only views.

### 1.2 schemars is mandatory and is the sole schema generator

Every struct that touches the Zeroclaw schema surface — `ZeroclawState`,
`LlmProjection`, `ModelRoute`, `Provider`, `Router`, `SelectorPolicy`,
`SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`, `ZeroclawError`,
absorbed provider adapter config structs — MUST derive
`schemars::JsonSchema`. This is not optional.

The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` field set is generated **entirely** from the
`schemars` output for `ZeroclawState` via the converter defined in §8. The
legacy `schema_from_state()` JSON-introspection path is **replaced** for
Zeroclaw. D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto field names, MCP tool parameter
schemas, and UI field renderers all derive from this one `schemars`-generated
JSON Schema. Any struct without `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` is invisible
to the system and cannot participate in the D-Bus/gRPC/MCP surface.

---

## 2. Schema Field Changes

### 2a. New fields on `ModelRoute`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`)

```rust
pub cost_profile:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.cost-profile@v1
pub effort_level:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.effort-level@v1
pub latency_class:     String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.latency-class@v1
pub privacy_tier:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1
pub context_window:    u32,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.context-window@v1
pub health_score:      f64,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1
pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1
pub tool_support:      Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1
```

`cost_profile` is the confirmed Zeroclaw-native cost field name (a budget-class
string, unit-neutral — **not** a per-token number). All new fields carry
`#[serde(default)]` and are visible to `schemars`.

### 2b. New top-level field on `ZeroclawState`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`)

```rust
pub selector_policy: SelectorPolicy,  // subid: sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1
```

### 2c. New struct `SelectorPolicy`

```rust
pub struct SelectorPolicy {
    pub effort_weight:        f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.effort-weight@v1
    pub cost_weight:          f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.cost-weight@v1
    pub latency_weight:       f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.latency-weight@v1
    pub health_weight:        f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.health-weight@v1
    pub default_effort:       String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-effort@v1
    pub default_privacy_tier: String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-privacy@v1
}
```

### 2d. New structs `SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`

Exposed as D-Bus method shapes and MCP tool parameters. All derive
`schemars::JsonSchema`.

```rust
pub struct SelectionInput {
    pub task_class:        String,
    pub requested_effort:  String,
    pub cost_policy:       Option<String>,   // budget class / cost ceiling policy
    pub latency_target:    Option<String>,
    pub context_tokens:    u32,
    pub privacy_tier:      String,
    pub tool_needs:        Vec<String>,
    pub explicit_provider: Option<String>,
    pub explicit_model:    Option<String>,
}   // subid: sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1

pub struct SelectionOutput {
    pub selected_provider: String,
    pub selected_model:    String,
    pub reason:            String,
    pub estimated_cost:    Option<String>,   // Zeroclaw-native units (unit-neutral)
    pub effort_level:      String,
    pub confidence:        f64,
    pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>,
    pub event_metadata:    SelectionEvent,
}   // subid: sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1

pub struct SelectionEvent {
    pub trace_id:         String,
    pub timestamp:        String,
    pub selector_version: String,
}   // subid: evt.service.zeroclaw.selection-event@v1
```

---

## 3. D-Bus Method/Property/Signal Shape

See design.md §3 for the full table. Implementation notes:

- All paths use the canonical prefix `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` and bus
  `org.opdbus.v1` (the convention used by `op-projection`, `op-state`, and
  `op-state-store`). The legacy `/opdbus/v1/...` string in `zeroclaw.rs`'s
  `transport` block is corrected to `/org/opdbus/v1/...` as part of T-11.
- `AuthorizeExecution` MUST check schema state atomically; it emits
  `ExecutionAuthorized` or `ExecutionDenied`.
- `SelectModel` runs the algorithm in design.md §4 using only `ZeroclawState`
  from the projection; no env reads.
- All mutation methods (`SetProvider`, `SetModel`, `SelectModel`) MUST carry
  `actor_id` in audit metadata and emit the corresponding signal.
- `ResolveRoute` is read-only (obs category); it does not mutate state.

---

## 4. Dynamic Model Selection Implementation

Location: new module
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/selector.rs`

```rust
pub fn select_model(
    input: &SelectionInput,
    state: &ZeroclawState,
) -> Result<SelectionOutput, ZeroclawError>
```

- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `state.projection.tools`.
- Reads `state.selector_policy` for weights.
- Phase 1 hard filters then Phase 2 scoring per design.md §4.
- Cost filter/scoring use the Zeroclaw-native `cost_profile` field (budget
  class). No `cost_per_token` or unit math.
- Returns `ZeroclawError::NoCandidateAfterFiltering` (or a specific hard-filter
  error) on failure.
- Pure function — no I/O, no env reads, deterministic given state.

---

## 5. Layer Boundaries

Two bad outcomes this spec explicitly prevents:
1. `op-llm` survives as a hidden authority under a new name.
2. `op-plugins` becomes a runtime blob mixing provider HTTP clients with schema authority.

### Layer 1 — Zeroclaw Contract Layer
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/{zeroclaw.rs, common/llm_projection.rs, plugin_schema_defs.rs}`

Owns: `ZeroclawState` and all schema types, the `schemars`-generated
`PluginSchema`, route/provider/selector declarations, OSCAL subids.
The schema IS the plugin; `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth.
Must NOT contain: provider HTTP clients, network adapters, wire-format parsing,
auth header construction, or D-Bus object registration.

### Layer 2 — Zeroclaw Orchestration Layer
`common/selector.rs` + D-Bus method handlers in `zeroclaw.rs`.

Owns: dynamic model selection, scoring, route resolution, execution
authorization, fallback planning, `MutationEngine` integration, trace/event
emission, handoff to provider adapters. Reads contract/state only through
`SchemaEngine`/`MutationEngine`/the projection. Does NOT implement wire formats.

### Layer 3 — Provider Adapter Layer
Execution-host module confirmed by the Provider Absorption spike (NOT inside the
`op-plugins` schema authority if that would mix runtime I/O with schema
ownership).

Owns: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenClaw / Factory / Kilocode / Opencode /
OpenRouter / GCloudADC wire formats, request/response conversion, streaming, auth
headers, network calls.

Hard constraints: cannot select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass
D-Bus, or execute undeclared routes. Takes only a schema-authorized execution
plan. Must not call back into Orchestration/Contract, read `/dev/shm`, or query
D-Bus for live state.

### Dependency direction (see §10 for crate-level rules)
```
Contract Layer   → defines schema; schemars generates PluginSchema
Orchestration    → consumes contract/state; produces execution plan
Provider Adapter → consumes execution plan; performs provider call
                   ✗ must not call back into Orchestration or Contract
```

---

## 6. Provider Adapter Absorption Plan

### 6a. Source inventory (`crates/op-llm/src/`)

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `provider.rs` | `LlmProvider` trait, `ChatMessage`, `ToolDefinition`, `ProviderType` |
| `chat.rs` | `ChatManager` — env-driven provider selection (to be replaced) |
| `anthropic.rs` | `AnthropicClient` |
| `gemini.rs` | `GeminiClient` |
| `gemini_cli.rs` | `create_gemini_cli_provider` |
| `factory.rs` | `FactoryProvider` |
| `openclaw.rs` | `OpenClawProvider` |
| `assistant.rs` | `AssistantProvider` |
| `gcloud_adc.rs` | `GCloudADCProvider` |

### 6b. Absorption target
Behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface, subordinate to Zeroclaw's schema authority.
Adapters MUST NOT become a second authority. The exact target module is
identified by the Provider Absorption spike (T-40) and recorded in
`handoff-provider-absorption.md` before any file moves. No new crate. Adapter
HTTP/runtime behavior must remain separate from `PluginSchema` authority.
Factory is a provider category in the catalog, not a separate D-Bus object.

Any config/options struct in the moved files (`AnthropicConfig`, `GeminiConfig`,
`OpenClawConfig`, …) MUST derive `schemars::JsonSchema` — they are
schema-contract types.

### 6c. `ChatManager` retirement
Replaced by the Zeroclaw D-Bus `SelectModel` + `AuthorizeExecution` flow.
Removed from the public API after callers are migrated.

### 6d. Compatibility shim
A thin `pub use` re-export in `op-llm` preserves `LlmProvider`/`ChatMessage` at
their old paths during Caller Migration; removed in the final task.

---

## 7. Single Projection Contract (`/dev/shm` is a snapshot, not an authority)

`SchemaEngine` (in `op-projection`) is the **sole writer** of any Zeroclaw
projection artifact and the **sole owner** of the in-memory `PluginSchema`.

### Lifecycle
1. `SchemaEngine` registers/holds the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`
   (generated from `schemars` per §8).
2. On schema/state change, `SchemaEngine`:
   a. notifies registered **projection observers** (§9) — the in-memory
      `PluginSchema` is passed by reference; this is how the D-Bus tree updates;
   b. writes the discovery snapshot `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`
      atomically (`.tmp` + `rename`);
   c. updates the aggregated `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` (and the catalog-hash
      manifest) in its existing aggregation pass.
3. Individual plugins NEVER write any `/dev/shm` file.

### Read path — strict
- The grpc-bridge builds the D-Bus tree from the **in-memory `PluginSchema`**
  passed by `SchemaEngine` to the observer — **never** by reading the
  `/dev/shm` JSON file.
- `op-chat` and MCP MUST use D-Bus for execution-path decisions.
- The `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` file is for discovery/inspection
  only. No consumer reads it on an execution path; no consumer writes it.

### Invariants
- Snapshot file absent → SchemaEngine hasn't registered Zeroclaw yet; the D-Bus
  tree is likewise absent; callers wait.
- Snapshot stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; it is non-authoritative anyway.

---

## 8. Schemars → `PluginSchema` Generation (replaces `schema_from_state` for Zeroclaw)

The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` is generated from `schemars`, not from JSON
introspection. Add to `plugin_schema_defs.rs`:

```rust
/// Convert a schemars RootSchema for a `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` type into the
/// runtime `PluginSchema` field set. Single generator for schema-contract types.
pub(crate) fn plugin_schema_from_schemars<T: schemars::JsonSchema>(
    name: &str,
    category: &str,
    version: &str,
    description: &str,
    methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>,
    signals: Vec<SignalDecl>,
    guarantees: PluginCapabilities,
    subids: HashMap<String, String>,
) -> PluginSchema;
```

- Internally calls `schemars::schema_for!(T)` and maps each top-level property
  in the generated JSON Schema to a `FieldSchema` (type, required, default,
  description), building the `PluginSchema` via `PluginSchemaBuilder`.
- `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` is rewritten to call
  `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<ZeroclawState>(...)` and supplies the declared
  `methods` (§3), `signals`, `guarantees`, and the `subids` map (§13).
- `schema_from_state()` remains for other plugins not yet migrated; it is **not**
  used for Zeroclaw.
- A `#[test]` asserts `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` contains
  `model_routes`, `providers`, `selector_policy`, `selection_input` (via method
  shapes), and `selection_output`, and that the produced `PluginSchema.fields`
  matches the schemars property set.

---

## 9. D-Bus Projection ↔ gRPC-Bridge Integration (the single call surface)

The grpc-bridge publishes the **one** Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` as a live D-Bus
object tree. It owns no projection of its own — it is an observer/view of
`SchemaEngine`. This is the primary call surface for Refactro and any
schema-driven consumer. HTTP/env reads for live execution state are prohibited.

### 9.1 Object tree

| D-Bus path | Contents | busctl example |
|---|---|---|
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` | `ZeroclawState` snapshot + methods | `busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw org.opdbus.v1 GetState` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` | one `ModelRoute` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` | one `Provider` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` |

`<hint>` is `ModelRoute.hint`; `<id>` is `Provider.id`.

### 9.2 Dependency direction — no cycle

`SchemaEngine` lives in `op-projection`; the bridge hook lives in
`op-grpc-bridge`. To avoid `op-projection → op-grpc-bridge → op-projection`:

- `op-projection` defines a trait (no new deps):
  ```rust
  pub trait SchemaProjectionObserver: Send + Sync {
      fn on_zeroclaw_projection(&self, schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState);
  }
  ```
  `SchemaEngine` holds `Vec<Arc<dyn SchemaProjectionObserver>>` and invokes them
  after each projection cycle.
- `op-grpc-bridge` depends on `op-projection` (one direction only) and provides
  `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook: SchemaProjectionObserver`. At startup the bridge
  registers its hook with `SchemaEngine::register_projection_observer(...)`.
- `op-projection` has **no** compile-time dependency on `op-grpc-bridge`.

### 9.3 `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook`
New type in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_projection.rs`:

```rust
pub struct GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    connection: zbus::Connection,
    // holds the last registered object set for diffing
}

impl SchemaProjectionObserver for GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    fn on_zeroclaw_projection(&self, schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState) { /* spawn apply */ }
}

impl GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    pub async fn apply_projection(&self, state: &ZeroclawState) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
}
```

- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `.providers` from the **in-memory**
  state handed in by the observer call — never from `/dev/shm`, env, or any
  other source.
- For each route/provider, registers a D-Bus object whose **property names and
  types are enumerated from `schemars::schema_for!(ModelRoute)` /
  `schema_for!(Provider)`** — not hardcoded strings.
- Diffs against the previous cycle: unregisters objects whose `hint`/`id` no
  longer appears.
- Registration failures (e.g. bus name not yet acquired) log a warning and retry
  on the next cycle; they never abort the SchemaEngine cycle.

### 9.4 gRPC streaming
`op-grpc-bridge`'s `SchemaPassthroughService` serves the same `PluginSchema`
view over `operation.v1.PluginService` as a `ZeroclawProjection` message
(`schema_json`, repeated `ModelRouteProto`, repeated `ProviderProto`) so remote
consumers (e.g. `cognitive-mcp` on WireGuard) subscribe without polling D-Bus.
This is a serialization of the same one schema, not a new projection.

### 9.5 Non-goals
- Refactro MUST NOT call `op-llm` HTTP endpoints directly.
- Refactro MUST NOT read `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` as live state;
  it uses D-Bus (§9.1) or the gRPC stream (§9.4).
- The grpc-bridge does NOT own model selection — it only projects what
  `SchemaEngine` registered. Selection flows through D-Bus `SelectModel` /
  `AuthorizeExecution` on the top-level plugin object.

---

## 10. Crate Dependency Direction (cycle prevention)

| Edge | Allowed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `op-grpc-bridge` → `op-projection` | ✅ | bridge observes SchemaEngine |
| `op-projection` → `op-grpc-bridge` | ❌ | would create a cycle; use the observer trait (§9.2) |
| `op-grpc-bridge` → `op-plugins` | ✅ | bridge reads `ZeroclawState`/schema types |
| `op-plugins` → `op-grpc-bridge` | ❌ | schema authority must not depend on the bridge |
| `op-plugins` (schema) → provider HTTP adapters | ❌ | Layer-1 must not own runtime I/O (§5) |

The observer trait and `ZeroclawState`/`PluginSchema` types are the only shared
surface across these crates.

---

## 11. `op-llm` Retirement Stages

| Stage | Action | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Inventory all callers of `op-llm` | `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` baseline |
| 1 | Schema Agent: schemars-type `ZeroclawState`; generate `PluginSchema` via §8 | `cargo check -p op-plugins` green |
| 1b | Bridge Agent: D-Bus tree via observer (§9) | `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge`; `busctl introspect` shows route objects |
| 2 | Provider Absorption: move adapters | `cargo check -p op-llm` still green (compat shim) |
| 3 | Router Agent: `select_model` | route-selection tests pass |
| 4 | Caller Migration: `op-chat`, `op-web`, factory | `rg 'op_llm::'` zero hits outside `op-llm` |
| 5 | Remove shim; remove `op-llm` from workspace | `cargo build --workspace` green without `op-llm` |

---

## 12. Multi-Agent Handoff Contract

Each agent deposits a handoff file in `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/`.
Every handoff MUST contain:

```markdown
## Scope Completed
## Files Changed
## Contract Changes  (new types, trait changes, D-Bus signatures)

```

| File | Agent |

| `handoff-schema.md` | Schema Agent |
| `handoff-bridge.md` | Bridge Agent |
| `handoff-dbus.md` | D-Bus Agent |
| `handoff-provider-absorption.md` | Provider Absorption Agent |
| `handoff-router.md` | Router Agent |
| `handoff-callers.md` | Caller Migration Agent |
| `handoff-projection.md` | Projection Agent |
| `handoff-tests.md` | Test Agent |
| `handoff-review.md` | Review Agent |

---

## 13. OSCAL Subid Mechanism + Registry

### 13.1 Mechanism (reconciled with the codebase)

The **single authority** for a subid is the `PluginSchema.subids:
HashMap<String, String>` map, keyed by field / method / signal name. This is the
