# Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm

---

## 1. Overview

Zeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for all LLM execution: provider catalog,
route resolution, model selection, tool-call translation, execution
authorization, and MCP/UI/gRPC exposure. This spec governs absorbing
`crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's plugin/schema/D-Bus architecture and retiring
`op-llm` as an independent crate.

**Primary authority file:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`

**Schema types (contract layer):**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`

**Schema re-export / `PluginSchema` builder:**
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`

**Single projection authority (producer):**
`crates/op-projection` → `SchemaEngine`

**D-Bus object tree (view, generated by the bridge):**
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` and children, on bus `org.opdbus.v1`

### 1.1 One projection — non-negotiable

There is **exactly one** projection of Zeroclaw, and it is owned by
`op-projection::SchemaEngine`. The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` (derived from
`ZeroclawState`) is the single source of truth. Everything else is a **view**
derived from that one schema, never a second computation:

- The **D-Bus object tree** under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/...` is a
  live view materialized by `op-grpc-bridge` directly from the in-memory
  `PluginSchema` held by `SchemaEngine` (§9). This is the primary call surface.
- The **`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`** file is a **non-authoritative
  discovery snapshot** written by `SchemaEngine` for human/tooling inspection.
  It is **never read back** to build the D-Bus tree, and **never** used for
  execution-path decisions (§7).
- The **gRPC stream** (`ZeroclawProjection`) is a serialized view of the same
  `PluginSchema`, for remote subscribers (§9.4).

No component computes, mutates, or re-derives the projection except
`SchemaEngine`. The bridge, the file, and the gRPC stream are read-only views.

### 1.2 schemars is mandatory and is the sole schema generator

Every struct that touches the Zeroclaw schema surface — `ZeroclawState`,
`LlmProjection`, `ModelRoute`, `Provider`, `Router`, `SelectorPolicy`,
`SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`, `ZeroclawError`,
absorbed provider adapter config structs — MUST derive
`schemars::JsonSchema`. This is not optional.

The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` field set is generated **entirely** from the
`schemars` output for `ZeroclawState` via the converter defined in §8. The
legacy `schema_from_state()` JSON-introspection path is **replaced** for
Zeroclaw. D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto field names, MCP tool parameter
schemas, and UI field renderers all derive from this one `schemars`-generated
JSON Schema. Any struct without `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` is invisible
to the system and cannot participate in the D-Bus/gRPC/MCP surface.

---

## 2. Schema Field Changes

### 2a. New fields on `ModelRoute`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`)

```rust
pub cost_profile:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.cost-profile@v1
pub effort_level:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.effort-level@v1
pub latency_class:     String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.latency-class@v1
pub privacy_tier:      String,      // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.privacy-tier@v1
pub context_window:    u32,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.context-window@v1
pub health_score:      f64,         // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.health-score@v1
pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.fallback-routes@v1
pub tool_support:      Vec<String>, // subid: obs.software.llm-model-route.tool-support@v1
```

`cost_profile` is the confirmed Zeroclaw-native cost field name (a budget-class
string, unit-neutral — **not** a per-token number). All new fields carry
`#[serde(default)]` and are visible to `schemars`.

### 2b. New top-level field on `ZeroclawState`
(in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`)

```rust
pub selector_policy: SelectorPolicy,  // subid: sch.software.zeroclaw.selector-policy@v1
```

### 2c. New struct `SelectorPolicy`

```rust
pub struct SelectorPolicy {
    pub effort_weight:        f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.effort-weight@v1
    pub cost_weight:          f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.cost-weight@v1
    pub latency_weight:       f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.latency-weight@v1
    pub health_weight:        f64,    // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.health-weight@v1
    pub default_effort:       String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-effort@v1
    pub default_privacy_tier: String, // subid: sch.software.selector-policy.default-privacy@v1
}
```

### 2d. New structs `SelectionInput`, `SelectionOutput`, `SelectionEvent`

Exposed as D-Bus method shapes and MCP tool parameters. All derive
`schemars::JsonSchema`.

```rust
pub struct SelectionInput {
    pub task_class:        String,
    pub requested_effort:  String,
    pub cost_policy:       Option<String>,   // budget class / cost ceiling policy
    pub latency_target:    Option<String>,
    pub context_tokens:    u32,
    pub privacy_tier:      String,
    pub tool_needs:        Vec<String>,
    pub explicit_provider: Option<String>,
    pub explicit_model:    Option<String>,
}   // subid: sch.software.llm-selection-input.schema@v1

pub struct SelectionOutput {
    pub selected_provider: String,
    pub selected_model:    String,
    pub reason:            String,
    pub estimated_cost:    Option<String>,   // Zeroclaw-native units (unit-neutral)
    pub effort_level:      String,
    pub confidence:        f64,
    pub fallback_routes:   Vec<String>,
    pub event_metadata:    SelectionEvent,
}   // subid: sch.software.llm-selection-output.schema@v1

pub struct SelectionEvent {
    pub trace_id:         String,
    pub timestamp:        String,
    pub selector_version: String,
}   // subid: evt.service.zeroclaw.selection-event@v1
```

---

## 3. D-Bus Method/Property/Signal Shape

See design.md §3 for the full table. Implementation notes:

- All paths use the canonical prefix `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` and bus
  `org.opdbus.v1` (the convention used by `op-projection`, `op-state`, and
  `op-state-store`). The legacy `/opdbus/v1/...` string in `zeroclaw.rs`'s
  `transport` block is corrected to `/org/opdbus/v1/...` as part of T-11.
- `AuthorizeExecution` MUST check schema state atomically; it emits
  `ExecutionAuthorized` or `ExecutionDenied`.
- `SelectModel` runs the algorithm in design.md §4 using only `ZeroclawState`
  from the projection; no env reads.
- All mutation methods (`SetProvider`, `SetModel`, `SelectModel`) MUST carry
  `actor_id` in audit metadata and emit the corresponding signal.
- `ResolveRoute` is read-only (obs category); it does not mutate state.

---

## 4. Dynamic Model Selection Implementation

Location: new module
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/selector.rs`

```rust
pub fn select_model(
    input: &SelectionInput,
    state: &ZeroclawState,
) -> Result<SelectionOutput, ZeroclawError>
```

- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `state.projection.tools`.
- Reads `state.selector_policy` for weights.
- Phase 1 hard filters then Phase 2 scoring per design.md §4.
- Cost filter/scoring use the Zeroclaw-native `cost_profile` field (budget
  class). No `cost_per_token` or unit math.
- Returns `ZeroclawError::NoCandidateAfterFiltering` (or a specific hard-filter
  error) on failure.
- Pure function — no I/O, no env reads, deterministic given state.

---

## 5. Layer Boundaries

Two bad outcomes this spec explicitly prevents:
1. `op-llm` survives as a hidden authority under a new name.
2. `op-plugins` becomes a runtime blob mixing provider HTTP clients with schema authority.

### Layer 1 — Zeroclaw Contract Layer
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/{zeroclaw.rs, common/llm_projection.rs, plugin_schema_defs.rs}`

Owns: `ZeroclawState` and all schema types, the `schemars`-generated
`PluginSchema`, route/provider/selector declarations, OSCAL subids.
The schema IS the plugin; `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth.
Must NOT contain: provider HTTP clients, network adapters, wire-format parsing,
auth header construction, or D-Bus object registration.

### Layer 2 — Zeroclaw Orchestration Layer
`common/selector.rs` + D-Bus method handlers in `zeroclaw.rs`.

Owns: dynamic model selection, scoring, route resolution, execution
authorization, fallback planning, `MutationEngine` integration, trace/event
emission, handoff to provider adapters. Reads contract/state only through
`SchemaEngine`/`MutationEngine`/the projection. Does NOT implement wire formats.

### Layer 3 — Provider Adapter Layer
Execution-host module confirmed by the Provider Absorption spike (NOT inside the
`op-plugins` schema authority if that would mix runtime I/O with schema
ownership).

Owns: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenClaw / Factory / Kilocode / Opencode /
OpenRouter / GCloudADC wire formats, request/response conversion, streaming, auth
headers, network calls.

Hard constraints: cannot select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass
D-Bus, or execute undeclared routes. Takes only a schema-authorized execution
plan. Must not call back into Orchestration/Contract, read `/dev/shm`, or query
D-Bus for live state.

### Dependency direction (see §10 for crate-level rules)
```
Contract Layer   → defines schema; schemars generates PluginSchema
Orchestration    → consumes contract/state; produces execution plan
Provider Adapter → consumes execution plan; performs provider call
                   ✗ must not call back into Orchestration or Contract
```

---

## 6. Provider Adapter Absorption Plan

### 6a. Source inventory (`crates/op-llm/src/`)

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `provider.rs` | `LlmProvider` trait, `ChatMessage`, `ToolDefinition`, `ProviderType` |
| `chat.rs` | `ChatManager` — env-driven provider selection (to be replaced) |
| `anthropic.rs` | `AnthropicClient` |
| `gemini.rs` | `GeminiClient` |
| `gemini_cli.rs` | `create_gemini_cli_provider` |
| `factory.rs` | `FactoryProvider` |
| `openclaw.rs` | `OpenClawProvider` |
| `assistant.rs` | `AssistantProvider` |
| `gcloud_adc.rs` | `GCloudADCProvider` |

### 6b. Absorption target
Behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface, subordinate to Zeroclaw's schema authority.
Adapters MUST NOT become a second authority. The exact target module is
identified by the Provider Absorption spike (T-40) and recorded in
`handoff-provider-absorption.md` before any file moves. No new crate. Adapter
HTTP/runtime behavior must remain separate from `PluginSchema` authority.
Factory is a provider category in the catalog, not a separate D-Bus object.

Any config/options struct in the moved files (`AnthropicConfig`, `GeminiConfig`,
`OpenClawConfig`, …) MUST derive `schemars::JsonSchema` — they are
schema-contract types.

### 6c. `ChatManager` retirement
Replaced by the Zeroclaw D-Bus `SelectModel` + `AuthorizeExecution` flow.
Removed from the public API after callers are migrated.

### 6d. Compatibility shim
A thin `pub use` re-export in `op-llm` preserves `LlmProvider`/`ChatMessage` at
their old paths during Caller Migration; removed in the final task.

---

## 7. Single Projection Contract (`/dev/shm` is a snapshot, not an authority)

`SchemaEngine` (in `op-projection`) is the **sole writer** of any Zeroclaw
projection artifact and the **sole owner** of the in-memory `PluginSchema`.

### Lifecycle
1. `SchemaEngine` registers/holds the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`
   (generated from `schemars` per §8).
2. On schema/state change, `SchemaEngine`:
   a. notifies registered **projection observers** (§9) — the in-memory
      `PluginSchema` is passed by reference; this is how the D-Bus tree updates;
   b. writes the discovery snapshot `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`
      atomically (`.tmp` + `rename`);
   c. updates the aggregated `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` (and the catalog-hash
      manifest) in its existing aggregation pass.
3. Individual plugins NEVER write any `/dev/shm` file.

### Read path — strict
- The grpc-bridge builds the D-Bus tree from the **in-memory `PluginSchema`**
  passed by `SchemaEngine` to the observer — **never** by reading the
  `/dev/shm` JSON file.
- `op-chat` and MCP MUST use D-Bus for execution-path decisions.
- The `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` file is for discovery/inspection
  only. No consumer reads it on an execution path; no consumer writes it.

### Invariants
- Snapshot file absent → SchemaEngine hasn't registered Zeroclaw yet; the D-Bus
  tree is likewise absent; callers wait.
- Snapshot stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; it is non-authoritative anyway.

---

## 8. Schemars → `PluginSchema` Generation (replaces `schema_from_state` for Zeroclaw)

The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` is generated from `schemars`, not from JSON
introspection. Add to `plugin_schema_defs.rs`:

```rust
/// Convert a schemars RootSchema for a `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` type into the
/// runtime `PluginSchema` field set. Single generator for schema-contract types.
pub(crate) fn plugin_schema_from_schemars<T: schemars::JsonSchema>(
    name: &str,
    category: &str,
    version: &str,
    description: &str,
    methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>,
    signals: Vec<SignalDecl>,
    guarantees: PluginCapabilities,
    subids: HashMap<String, String>,
) -> PluginSchema;
```

- Internally calls `schemars::schema_for!(T)` and maps each top-level property
  in the generated JSON Schema to a `FieldSchema` (type, required, default,
  description), building the `PluginSchema` via `PluginSchemaBuilder`.
- `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` is rewritten to call
  `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<ZeroclawState>(...)` and supplies the declared
  `methods` (§3), `signals`, `guarantees`, and the `subids` map (§13).
- `schema_from_state()` remains for other plugins not yet migrated; it is **not**
  used for Zeroclaw.
- A `#[test]` asserts `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` contains
  `model_routes`, `providers`, `selector_policy`, `selection_input` (via method
  shapes), and `selection_output`, and that the produced `PluginSchema.fields`
  matches the schemars property set.

---

## 9. D-Bus Projection ↔ gRPC-Bridge Integration (the single call surface)

The grpc-bridge publishes the **one** Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` as a live D-Bus
object tree. It owns no projection of its own — it is an observer/view of
`SchemaEngine`. This is the primary call surface for Refactro and any
schema-driven consumer. HTTP/env reads for live execution state are prohibited.

### 9.1 Object tree

| D-Bus path | Contents | busctl example |
|---|---|---|
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` | `ZeroclawState` snapshot + methods | `busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw org.opdbus.v1 GetState` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` | one `ModelRoute` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` |
| `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` | one `Provider` | `busctl introspect org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>` |

`<hint>` is `ModelRoute.hint`; `<id>` is `Provider.id`.

### 9.2 Dependency direction — no cycle

`SchemaEngine` lives in `op-projection`; the bridge hook lives in
`op-grpc-bridge`. To avoid `op-projection → op-grpc-bridge → op-projection`:

- `op-projection` defines a trait (no new deps):
  ```rust
  pub trait SchemaProjectionObserver: Send + Sync {
      fn on_zeroclaw_projection(&self, schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState);
  }
  ```
  `SchemaEngine` holds `Vec<Arc<dyn SchemaProjectionObserver>>` and invokes them
  after each projection cycle.
- `op-grpc-bridge` depends on `op-projection` (one direction only) and provides
  `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook: SchemaProjectionObserver`. At startup the bridge
  registers its hook with `SchemaEngine::register_projection_observer(...)`.
- `op-projection` has **no** compile-time dependency on `op-grpc-bridge`.

### 9.3 `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook`
New type in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_projection.rs`:

```rust
pub struct GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    connection: zbus::Connection,
    // holds the last registered object set for diffing
}

impl SchemaProjectionObserver for GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    fn on_zeroclaw_projection(&self, schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState) { /* spawn apply */ }
}

impl GrpcBridgeProjectionHook {
    pub async fn apply_projection(&self, state: &ZeroclawState) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
}
```

- Reads `state.projection.model_routes` and `.providers` from the **in-memory**
  state handed in by the observer call — never from `/dev/shm`, env, or any
  other source.
- For each route/provider, registers a D-Bus object whose **property names and
  types are enumerated from `schemars::schema_for!(ModelRoute)` /
  `schema_for!(Provider)`** — not hardcoded strings.
- Diffs against the previous cycle: unregisters objects whose `hint`/`id` no
  longer appears.
- Registration failures (e.g. bus name not yet acquired) log a warning and retry
  on the next cycle; they never abort the SchemaEngine cycle.

### 9.4 gRPC streaming
`op-grpc-bridge`'s `SchemaPassthroughService` serves the same `PluginSchema`
view over `operation.v1.PluginService` as a `ZeroclawProjection` message
(`schema_json`, repeated `ModelRouteProto`, repeated `ProviderProto`) so remote
consumers (e.g. `cognitive-mcp` on WireGuard) subscribe without polling D-Bus.
This is a serialization of the same one schema, not a new projection.

### 9.5 Non-goals
- Refactro MUST NOT call `op-llm` HTTP endpoints directly.
- Refactro MUST NOT read `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` as live state;
  it uses D-Bus (§9.1) or the gRPC stream (§9.4).
- The grpc-bridge does NOT own model selection — it only projects what
  `SchemaEngine` registered. Selection flows through D-Bus `SelectModel` /
  `AuthorizeExecution` on the top-level plugin object.

| Edge | Allowed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `op-grpc-bridge` → `op-projection` | ✅ | bridge observes SchemaEngine |
| `op-projection` → `op-grpc-bridge` | ❌ | would create a cycle; use the observer trait (§9.2) |

surface across these crates.

## 13. OSCAL Subid Mechanism + Registry

### 13.1 Mechanism (reconciled with the codebase)

The **single authority** for a subid is the `PluginSchema.subids:
HashMap<String, String>` map, keyed by field / method / signal name. This is the
existing codebase convention and what the registry, renderer, and compliance
overlays read. Zeroclaw's `subids` map is supplied to
`plugin_schema_from_schemars` (§8) and is the place a reviewer/tool reads to
verify coverage and uniqueness.

`schemars` field-level extension annotations (`x-oscal-subid`) are **not** used
(schemars 0.8 cannot emit arbitrary extension keys reliably). Source-level
`// subid:` doc comments on struct fields are advisory markers only; they are
**not** the authority. The Review gate (T-80) therefore checks the **generated
`PluginSchema.subids` map** for completeness and value-uniqueness, **not** raw
`x-oscal-subid` source literals.

content.text:
Good instinct — and yes, that's my recommendation. I already baked it into the rewritten spec (§8), so let me confirm the reasoning, then finish tasks.md + the mission.

## Recommendation for #3: emit from schemars (with one precise boundary)

**Yes — generate the `PluginSchema` *field set* from `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)`, replacing `schema_from_state()` for Zeroclaw.** Reasoning:

- `schema_from_state()` introspects a serialized **instance**, so it infers types from example *values* — an empty `Vec`, a `null`, a `0` all produce loose/wrong types, and optional-vs-required and nested struct shapes are lost. That's fine for a loose display schema, but Zeroclaw can't "fully function" on it: the D-Bus method arg/return shapes, MCP tool params, gRPC proto fields, and the per-route D-Bus property types in §9.3 (`schema_for!(ModelRoute)`) all need the **real declared contract**, not value-inferred guesses.
- schemars emits the true types, defaults, required/optional, and nested `$defs`. Making the typed structs the generator is also what enforces "the schema is the plugin" — *adding a field to `ZeroclawState` is the only way to change the schema.*

**The boundary that matters:** schemars describes **data shape**, not the **RPC verb set**. A D-Bus method (`SelectModel`) isn't a field of `ZeroclawState`. So the converter is:

> `PluginSchema.fields` ← `schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` (generated)
> `+ methods / signals / guarantees / subids` ← explicit declarations passed in

…and even the **method shapes** stay schemars-driven, because `SelectionInput`/`SelectionOutput` derive `JsonSchema` and the method decl references their `schema_for!`. Only the verb list and the subid→name mapping are hand-declared (they have nowhere else to live).

**The real cost** (and the one new work item): the converter must map JSON Schema → the codebase's `FieldSchema`/`FieldType` model, including `$ref`/`$defs` for nested structs, arrays, and `Option`. I scoped it as `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<T>()` in §8 and keep `schema_from_state()` for the ~30 other un-typed plugins — so this flips Zeroclaw only, incrementally.

### T-16: Wire hook into SchemaEngine projection cycle

**Agent:** Bridge
**File:** `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_router.rs` or `schema_engine.rs`

2. The hook runs async in the same projection task — no separate thread.
3. If hook registration fails (e.g., D-Bus name not yet acquired), log warning

### T-16: Wire hook via the `SchemaProjectionObserver` trait (no crate cycle)

**Agent:** Bridge
**Files:** `crates/op-projection/src/…` (trait + registry), `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/zeroclaw_projection.rs`
**Actions:**
1. Define `pub trait SchemaProjectionObserver { fn on_zeroclaw_projection(&self,
   schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState); }` in `op-projection` (spec
   §9.2). `SchemaEngine` holds `Vec<Arc<dyn SchemaProjectionObserver>>` and a
   `register_projection_observer(...)`; it invokes observers **after** each
   projection cycle, passing the **in-memory** `PluginSchema`/`ZeroclawState` —
   NOT a re-read of `/dev/shm`.
2. `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` implements `SchemaProjectionObserver`; on callback
   it spawns `apply_projection(state)`. The bridge registers its hook at startup.
3. `op-grpc-bridge` depends on `op-projection` only — `op-projection` MUST NOT
   depend on `op-grpc-bridge` (spec §10). Verify no new cycle.
4. Registration/D-Bus failures log a warning and retry next cycle; never abort
   the SchemaEngine cycle. The `/dev/shm` snapshot is never on this path.

**Verification:**
```bash
cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge
cargo check -p op-projection   # confirm no op-grpc-bridge dependency edge

input.content:
# Factory Mission: Absorb `op-llm` into Zeroclaw (schemars-native, single-projection)

## Mission
Implement the spec at `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/`
(`requirements.md`, `design.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`). Fold `crates/op-llm`
into the **Zeroclaw plugin** so that Zeroclaw becomes the single
schema/D-Bus/gRPC authority for all LLM execution — provider catalog, model
routes, dynamic selection, execution authorization — and retire `op-llm` as an
independent crate.

`tasks.md` is the authoritative, dependency-ordered work breakdown (T-00 →
T-90). The workspace must build at each phase gate. Every task carries its
verification commands — honor them.

The two design pillars this mission exists to enforce:

1. **schemars is the sole schema generator.** The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` is
   produced **entirely** from `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` via the
   `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<T>()` converter (spec §8) — `schema_from_state()`
   is **not** used for Zeroclaw. Every schema-surface struct derives
   `schemars::JsonSchema`. D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto fields, MCP tool
   params, UI renderers, and the per-route/per-provider D-Bus property types all
   derive from that one schemars output. A struct without `JsonSchema` is
   invisible and cannot route.

2. **Exactly one projection, owned by `op-projection::SchemaEngine`.** The D-Bus
   object tree under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/...` is a **view** the
   grpc-bridge materializes from the **in-memory** `PluginSchema` handed to it
   via the `SchemaProjectionObserver` trait (spec §9). `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/
   zeroclaw.json` is a non-authoritative discovery snapshot — written by
   SchemaEngine, **never read back** to build the tree or make execution
   decisions. There is no second projection and no recomputation.

## Method: TDD-orchestrated multi-agent
Use the enabled skills: `tdd-orchestrator`, `test-automator`,
`spec-to-code-compliance`, `rust-pro`, `rust-async-patterns`,
`systems-programming-rust-project`, `orchestrate-batch-refactor`.

For each task group: **RED** (write tests from the spec's acceptance criteria;
they must fail first) → **GREEN** (minimum to pass) → **REFACTOR** (keep the
workspace compiling) → **VERIFY** (`spec-to-code-compliance` against the task's
verification block) before advancing. Each agent deposits its handoff file
(`handoff-*.md`, spec §12) before the next phase proceeds.

## Orchestration (workstreams → phases in `tasks.md`)
Parallelize within a workstream; gate between them on a green `cargo check` of
the named crates.

- **WS0 — Baseline** (T-00, Coordinator): inventory `op_llm::` consumers
  (24 files across op-chat/op-web/op-mcp-proxy) + the 4 `Cargo.toml` deps; record
  `cargo build/test` baseline; commit `[baseline]`.
- **WS1 — Schema, schemars-native** (T-10…T-13, Schema Agent): typed
  `ZeroclawState`/`LlmProjection`/`ModelRoute`/`Provider`/`SelectorPolicy`/
  `Selection{Input,Output,Event}`/`ZeroclawError`, all deriving `JsonSchema`;
  add the `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<ZeroclawState>()` converter and rewrite
  `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` to use it; subids live in the `PluginSchema.subids`
  map (spec §13.1); golden test asserts fields == schemars properties + unique
  subids. Gate: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green.
- **WS1b — Bridge D-Bus projection** (T-15…T-18, Bridge Agent): define
  `SchemaProjectionObserver` in `op-projection`; `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook`
  in `op-grpc-bridge` registers one D-Bus object per route/provider with
  property names **enumerated from `schema_for!(ModelRoute)`/`schema_for!(Provider)`**
  (no hardcoded field strings); diff-based register/unregister; `ZeroclawProjection`
  proto + `SchemaPassthroughService` stream. `op-projection` MUST NOT depend on
  `op-grpc-bridge`. Gate: `busctl introspect …/zeroclaw/routes` shows objects.
- **WS2 — D-Bus methods** (T-20…T-22, D-Bus Agent): `ResolveRoute`,
  `GetModelRoutes`, `GetProviderCatalog`, `GetTools` (read), `SelectModel`,
  `AuthorizeExecution`, `SetProvider`, `SetModel` (mutation via `MutationEngine`,
  with `actor_id` + signals). Method shapes from schemars.
- **WS3 — Dynamic router** (T-30…T-31, Router Agent): pure
  `selector::select_model(&SelectionInput, &ZeroclawState) -> Result<…, ZeroclawError>`
  — Phase-1 hard filters + Phase-2 scoring, no `match` on provider/model name,
  `cost_profile` (budget class) only, no `cost_per_token`.
- **WS4 — Provider absorption** (T-40…T-42, Absorption Agent): spike to confirm

# Factory Mission: Absorb `op-llm` into Zeroclaw (schemars-native, single-projection)

## Mission
Implement the spec at `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/`
(`requirements.md`, `design.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`). Fold `crates/op-llm`
into the **Zeroclaw plugin** so that Zeroclaw becomes the single
schema/D-Bus/gRPC authority for all LLM execution — provider catalog, model
routes, dynamic selection, execution authorization — and retire `op-llm` as an
independent crate.

`tasks.md` is the authoritative, dependency-ordered work breakdown (T-00 →
T-90). The workspace must build at each phase gate. Every task carries its
verification commands — honor them.

The two design pillars this mission exists to enforce:

1. **schemars is the sole schema generator.** The Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` is
   produced **entirely** from `schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)` via the
   `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<T>()` converter (spec §8) — `schema_from_state()`
   is **not** used for Zeroclaw. Every schema-surface struct derives
   `schemars::JsonSchema`. D-Bus method shapes, gRPC proto fields, MCP tool
   params, UI renderers, and the per-route/per-provider D-Bus property types all
   derive from that one schemars output. A struct without `JsonSchema` is
   invisible and cannot route.

2. **Exactly one projection, owned by `op-projection::SchemaEngine`.** The D-Bus
   object tree under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/...` is a **view** the
   grpc-bridge materializes from the **in-memory** `PluginSchema` handed to it
   via the `SchemaProjectionObserver` trait (spec §9). `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/
   zeroclaw.json` is a non-authoritative discovery snapshot — written by
   SchemaEngine, **never read back** to build the tree or make execution
   decisions. There is no second projection and no recomputation.

## Method: TDD-orchestrated multi-agent
Use the enabled skills: `tdd-orchestrator`, `test-automator`,
`spec-to-code-compliance`, `rust-pro`, `rust-async-patterns`,
`systems-programming-rust-project`, `orchestrate-batch-refactor`.

For each task group: **RED** (write tests from the spec's acceptance criteria;
they must fail first) → **GREEN** (minimum to pass) → **REFACTOR** (keep the
workspace compiling) → **VERIFY** (`spec-to-code-compliance` against the task's
verification block) before advancing. Each agent deposits its handoff file
(`handoff-*.md`, spec §12) before the next phase proceeds.

## Orchestration (workstreams → phases in `tasks.md`)
Parallelize within a workstream; gate between them on a green `cargo check` of
the named crates.

- **WS0 — Baseline** (T-00, Coordinator): inventory `op_llm::` consumers
  (24 files across op-chat/op-web/op-mcp-proxy) + the 4 `Cargo.toml` deps; record
  `cargo build/test` baseline; commit `[baseline]`.
- **WS1 — Schema, schemars-native** (T-10…T-13, Schema Agent): typed
  `ZeroclawState`/`LlmProjection`/`ModelRoute`/`Provider`/`SelectorPolicy`/
  `Selection{Input,Output,Event}`/`ZeroclawError`, all deriving `JsonSchema`;
  add the `plugin_schema_from_schemars::<ZeroclawState>()` converter and rewrite
  `zeroclaw_plugin_schema()` to use it; subids live in the `PluginSchema.subids`
  map (spec §13.1); golden test asserts fields == schemars properties + unique
  subids. Gate: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green.
- **WS1b — Bridge D-Bus projection** (T-15…T-18, Bridge Agent): define
  `SchemaProjectionObserver` in `op-projection`; `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook`
  in `op-grpc-bridge` registers one D-Bus object per route/provider with
  property names **enumerated from `schema_for!(ModelRoute)`/`schema_for!(Provider)`**
  (no hardcoded field strings); diff-based register/unregister; `ZeroclawProjection`
  proto + `SchemaPassthroughService` stream. `op-projection` MUST NOT depend on
  `op-grpc-bridge`. Gate: `busctl introspect …/zeroclaw/routes` shows objects.
- **WS2 — D-Bus methods** (T-20…T-22, D-Bus Agent): `ResolveRoute`,
  `GetModelRoutes`, `GetProviderCatalog`, `GetTools` (read), `SelectModel`,
  `AuthorizeExecution`, `SetProvider`, `SetModel` (mutation via `MutationEngine`,
  with `actor_id` + signals). Method shapes from schemars.
- **WS3 — Dynamic router** (T-30…T-31, Router Agent): pure
  `selector::select_model(&SelectionInput, &ZeroclawState) -> Result<…, ZeroclawError>`
  — Phase-1 hard filters + Phase-2 scoring, no `match` on provider/model name,
  `cost_profile` (budget class) only, no `cost_per_token`.
- **WS4 — Provider absorption** (T-40…T-42, Absorption Agent): spike to confirm
  the execution-host module (record in `handoff-provider-absorption.md`); move
  the 9 adapter files; config structs derive `JsonSchema`; compat `pub use` shim
  in `op-llm`. No new crate.
- **WS5 — Caller migration & retirement** (T-50…T-53, Caller Agent): migrate
  op-chat, op-web, factory routes, remaining callers to the Zeroclaw D-Bus
  surface; remove the shim; drop `op-llm` from workspace members.
- **WS6 — Projection/Test/Review** (T-60…T-90): single-projection verification,
  undeclared-route enforcement, subid uniqueness, full bypass audit, acceptance.

## Hard rules (do not violate — these are why naïve attempts fail here)
- **schemars or it doesn't exist.** Never hand-build a `PluginSchema` field set
  for Zeroclaw, never reach for `schema_from_state()` here, never `impl JsonSchema`
  manually for a contract type. Adding a field to `ZeroclawState` is the ONLY way
  to change the schema.
- **One projection, one writer.** Only `SchemaEngine` writes projection
  artifacts. The bridge/file/gRPC stream are read-only **views** of the one
  in-memory `PluginSchema`. Never read `/dev/shm` on an execution or
  object-registration path. Never recompute the schema in a consumer.
- **No crate cycle.** `op-grpc-bridge → op-projection` only; the observer trait
  is the seam. `op-plugins` (schema authority) never depends on `op-grpc-bridge`
  and never owns provider HTTP clients.
- **No stubs, no placeholders, no "for now".** A registered D-Bus object that
  returns fake success, or `AuthorizeExecution` that validates against an empty
  set, is a defect. Inert code that *looks* wired is the recurring failure mode.
- **Nothing executes that isn't declared.** No undeclared provider/model/route/
  tool may run. No static `match effort {…}` model picker. Factory is a provider
  category in the catalog — never a second D-Bus object or BYOM control plane.
- **Canonical addressing only:** bus `org.opdbus.v1`, paths
  `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw[/routes/<hint>|/providers/<id>]`. Fix the
  legacy `/opdbus/v1/...` transport string in `zeroclaw.rs`.

## Definition of done
`cargo build --workspace` green **without** `op-llm`; `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'`
empty; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
clean; `cargo test --workspace` green; all nine `handoff-*.md` present;
`busctl` can `GetModelRoutes` / `SelectModel` / `AuthorizeExecution` and
introspect the route/provider sub-objects.

truth for D-Bus method generation, MCP tool declarations, gRPC shape
derivation, and UI field rendering. `SchemaEngine` owns schema
registration and projection; `MutationEngine` owns validated state mutations

gRPC bridge refactor — per-plugin hand-written D-Bus plumbing is not required.

```

          ├─ selected_model: String
          ├─ transport: LlmTransport
          └─ selector_policy: SelectorPolicy  ← new
```

The schema is generated by `schemars` from these types. It is re-exported
through `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. If a provider/model/tool/route is not in this
schema projection, it does not exist and cannot execute.

222	## 6. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract
223	
224	```
225	/dev/shm/
226	  live-schema.json               ← written by SchemaEngine (aggregates all plugin schemas)
227	  opdbus/
228	    schemas/
229	      zeroclaw.json              ← derived PluginSchema projection written by SchemaEngine
230	      antigravity.json           ← derived PluginSchema projection for other plugins
231	      ...
232	```
233	
234	`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is a **derived `PluginSchema`
235	projection** — a JSON snapshot of the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` as registered
236	and maintained by `SchemaEngine`. It is NOT a serialized live `ZeroclawState`
237	file. `SchemaEngine` owns schema registration and writes derived schema
238	catalogs. `MutationEngine` owns validated state mutations against `PluginSchema`.
239	
240	- **`SchemaEngine` is the sole writer** of `schemas/zeroclaw.json`.
241	- The file is written atomically (write to `.tmp`, then `rename`).
242	- `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` is written by `SchemaEngine`'s aggregation pass
243	  and combines all plugin schemas. Individual plugins do NOT write it.
244	- Consumers (`op-grpc-bridge`, factory provider routes) MAY read these files
245	  for discovery and display. They MUST NOT treat them as live mutable state.
246	- `op-chat` and MCP surfaces MUST use D-Bus, not `/dev/shm` reads, for
247	  execution-path decisions.
248

## 6. Single Projection + gRPC-Bridge D-Bus View

There is **exactly one** projection of Zeroclaw, owned by
`op-projection::SchemaEngine` (the `ShmWriter` introduced in PR #14). The D-Bus
object tree, the `/dev/shm` files, and the gRPC stream are all **views** of that
one in-memory `PluginSchema` — never a second computation or a second writer.
Full normative detail is in **spec §1.1, §7, §9, §10**; this section is the
design summary.

```
op-projection::SchemaEngine  (sole owner of the in-memory PluginSchema)
   │
   ├─(view A) GrpcBridgeProjectionHook → D-Bus object tree  ← PRIMARY call surface
   │            /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw[/routes/<hint>|/providers/<id>]
   ├─(view B) ShmWriter → /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json   ← discovery snapshot only
   │            + /dev/shm/live-schema.json (aggregate)            ← never read back on any path
   └─(view C) SchemaPassthroughService → gRPC ZeroclawProjection   ← remote subscribers
```

### Observer wiring (no crate cycle)
`SchemaEngine` lives in `op-projection`; the bridge hook lives in
`op-grpc-bridge`. To keep the dependency edge one-directional
(`op-grpc-bridge → op-projection`):

- `op-projection` defines `trait SchemaProjectionObserver { fn
  on_zeroclaw_projection(&self, schema: &PluginSchema, state: &ZeroclawState); }`
  and `SchemaEngine` invokes registered observers after each projection cycle,
  passing the **in-memory** schema/state.
- `op-grpc-bridge`'s `GrpcBridgeProjectionHook` implements the trait and is
  registered at startup. `op-projection` has **no** dependency on
  `op-grpc-bridge`.

### `/dev/shm` is a snapshot, not an authority
- **`SchemaEngine`/`ShmWriter` is the sole writer**; writes are atomic
  (`.tmp` + `rename`). Individual plugins NEVER write any `/dev/shm` file.
- The D-Bus tree is built from the in-memory `PluginSchema` handed to the
  observer — **never** by reading `zeroclaw.json` back.
- `op-chat`, MCP, and Refactro use D-Bus (or the gRPC stream) for execution-path
  decisions. The `/dev/shm` file is discovery/inspection only.

**Invariants:**
- Snapshot absent → SchemaEngine hasn't registered Zeroclaw; the D-Bus tree is
  likewise absent; callers wait.
- Snapshot stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; it is non-authoritative anyway.

## 4. Automatic Model Selection Algorithm

Input (`SelectionInput`):

```
task_class:          String         // "code", "chat", "reasoning", "vision", ...
requested_effort:    String         // "low", "medium", "high", "max"
cost_ceiling:        Option<f64>    // USD per 1M tokens; None = no limit
latency_target:      Option<String> // "interactive", "batch", None
context_tokens:      u32            // estimated token count
privacy_tier:        String         // "public", "internal", "confidential"
tool_needs:          Vec<String>    // tool names required
explicit_provider:   Option<String> // authorized override
explicit_model:      Option<String> // authorized override
```

Phase 1 — Hard Filters (applied in order, all must pass):

1. Route declared in `model_routes[]` — else reject.
2. `available == true` — else skip.
3. `privacy_tier` ≤ request tier — else skip.
4. Tool needs satisfied (`tools[]` declared) — else skip.
5. `context_window ≥ context_tokens` — else skip.
6. Route's cost profile satisfies the request cost policy (if a cost ceiling is
   set) — exact field names confirmed by Schema Agent spike against Zeroclaw's
   existing cost model; use placeholder `cost_profile`/`cost_policy` until
   confirmed.

Phase 2 — Scoring (higher = better, all values from schema state):

```
score = capability_match_bonus
      + effort_quality_score(route.effort_level, requested_effort)
      - cost_weight * <zeroclaw_cost_field>   // field name confirmed by Schema Agent
      - latency_penalty(route.latency_class, latency_target)
      + route_health_bonus(route.available, route.health_score)
```

The `cost_weight` coefficient and the exact cost field name come from
Zeroclaw's existing cost model schema. The Schema Agent MUST inspect
Zeroclaw's existing config/cost schema before naming the field in code.
Placeholder: `estimated_cost`.

Phase 3 — Output (`SelectionOutput`):

```
selected_provider:  String
selected_model:     String
reason:             String
estimated_cost:     <zeroclaw_cost_type>  // type/field confirmed by Schema Agent
effort_level:       String
confidence:         f64        // 0.0–1.0
fallback_routes:    Vec<String>  // ordered hints of next-best routes
event_metadata:     { trace_id, timestamp, selector_version }
```

The algorithm reads exclusively from `ZeroclawState` fields projected via
D-Bus. No `match` arm on `ProviderType` enum in the selection path.

# Requirements — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm

Feature: Zeroclaw absorbs `op-llm` and becomes the sole dynamic authority for LLM
routing, provider execution, model selection, tool-call translation, and
schema-driven execution authorization.

---

## REQ-01 — Zeroclaw is the single source of truth for all LLM execution

**WHEN** any component needs a provider, model, route, tool declaration, or
execution authorization,
**THEN** it MUST query the Zeroclaw D-Bus object at
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` (bus `org.opdbus.v1`).

Acceptance criteria:
- No caller resolves a provider or model outside of a Zeroclaw D-Bus read.
- No fallback to environment-variable provider selection in plugin/service code
  after migration is complete (bootstrap scripts remain the sole exception).
- `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` produces zero hits outside `op-llm` itself
  after Caller Migration is complete.

---

## REQ-02 — Provider/model/tool/route must be declared in Zeroclaw PluginSchema

**WHEN** any component attempts to execute an LLM call,
**THEN** the selected provider, model, route, and any tool being invoked MUST be
present in the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` as projected via D-Bus.

Acceptance criteria:
- A call with a provider/model combination absent from `model_routes` MUST be
  rejected with `Err` before any network I/O.
- A tool call whose `name` does not appear in `tools[]` in the schema MUST be
  rejected.
- Tests demonstrate that attempts to execute undeclared routes return
  `RouteNotDeclared` errors.

---

## REQ-03 — Dynamic automatic model selection

**WHEN** a caller supplies task metadata (task class, effort, cost ceiling,
latency target, context requirement, privacy tier, tool needs),
**THEN** Zeroclaw MUST select provider and model entirely from live
schema/D-Bus state with no static match tables in Rust.

Acceptance criteria:
- The selector reads only from Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` fields projected at
  runtime; no `match provider_type` arms in the selection path.
- Hard filter: routes where `available == false` or `privacy_tier` violates the
  request MUST be excluded before scoring.
- Scoring order: capability match → quality/effort → cost → latency → route
  health.
- Output includes: `selected_provider`, `selected_model`, `reason`,
  `estimated_cost`, `effort_level`, `confidence`, `fallback_routes[]`,
  `event_metadata`.
- Tests cover: lowest-cost-wins, effort-ceiling-respected,
  unavailable-route-excluded, privacy-tier-enforced.

---

## REQ-04 — `op-llm` provider adapters absorbed into Zeroclaw architecture

**WHEN** migration is complete,
**THEN** the provider execution adapters currently in
`crates/op-llm/src/{anthropic,gemini,gemini_cli,factory,openclaw,assistant,gcloud_adc}.rs`
MUST live inside the existing crate boundary that preserves Zeroclaw
plugin/D-Bus/schema authority, with no duplicate authority crate.

Acceptance criteria:
- `op-llm` is removed from workspace `Cargo.toml` after callers are migrated.
- `cargo build --workspace` passes with `op-llm` removed.
- All adapter behavior (OpenAI-compatible chat, tool-call translation,
  Anthropic content-block format, streaming, GCloud ADC) is preserved.

---

## REQ-05 — D-Bus is the only control plane

**WHEN** any plugin or service code reads or writes provider selection,
route selection, model availability, tool declarations, policy metadata, or
execution authorization,
**THEN** it MUST do so through D-Bus methods/properties on
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`.

Acceptance criteria:
- No `Command::new("...")` invocations for live state in plugin or service code.
- No direct live-state file reads outside bootstrap scripts.
- No JSON-RPC polling loops or D-Bus watchers for live state.

---

## REQ-06 — `/dev/shm/opdbus` files are derived projection artifacts, not authorities

**WHEN** `SchemaEngine` projects Zeroclaw to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`,
**THEN** that file MUST be a snapshot of the D-Bus-authoritative schema, not
the source of truth. Consumer reads of that file MUST NOT mutate it.

Acceptance criteria:
- `SchemaEngine` is the sole writer of `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.
- The monolithic all-plugin catalog at
  `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` is written by the schema
  aggregation layer, not by individual plugins.
- No consumer reads `/dev/shm` paths for live state decisions.

---

## REQ-07 — OSCAL subids on every new artifact

**WHEN** any new schema field, D-Bus method, mutation record, event, or MCP
tool is added,
**THEN** it MUST carry an `x-oscal-subid` annotation using one of the seven
categories (`src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`) per AGENTS.md
§4a.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI subid uniqueness check passes.
- No new field or method exists without a registered subid.

---

## REQ-08 — `op-chat`, `op-web`, MCP surfaces, and factory provider routes migrate off `op-llm`

**WHEN** migration is complete,
**THEN** `op-chat`, `op-web`, cognitive-mcp, and factory provider route code MUST
NOT import `op-llm` traits or types for provider selection or execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- `op-chat` calls Zeroclaw D-Bus for provider/model resolution before sending.
- Factory provider routes are declared in Zeroclaw's provider catalog. Factory
  BYOM discovery reads `model_routes[]` from Zeroclaw schema projection
  (D-Bus or `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`). Factory is a provider
  category within Zeroclaw's schema, not a separate D-Bus control object.
- `cognitive-mcp` remains the external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback
  only — neither is changed by this refactor.

---

## REQ-09 — No new crate, no new shim service

**WHEN** implementing this refactor,
**THEN** no new `op-zeroclaw` crate and no new shim/proxy service MUST be
introduced.

Acceptance criteria:
- Workspace `Cargo.toml` member count does not increase.
- No new binary service is registered with s6.

---

## REQ-11 — Three-layer boundary: Contract, Orchestration, Provider Adapter

**WHEN** provider adapters are absorbed and Zeroclaw execution logic is structured,
**THEN** the implementation MUST maintain three distinct layers with the dependency
direction: Contract → Orchestration → Provider Adapter (no back-calls).

Acceptance criteria:
- **Contract Layer** (`op-plugins` schema types): owns `PluginSchema`, `ZeroclawState`, schema
  declarations, OSCAL subids, generated D-Bus surface. Contains no HTTP client code.
- **Orchestration Layer** (selector, D-Bus method handlers, MutationEngine integration): reads
  state only through SchemaEngine/MutationEngine/D-Bus; does not implement provider wire formats.
- **Provider Adapter Layer** (absorbed adapter files): owns wire formats, streaming parsing, auth
  headers, network calls; takes only a schema-authorized execution plan from the Orchestration
  Layer. Does not select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass D-Bus, or call back into
  Orchestration.
- Provider adapters are NOT placed inside `op-plugins` if doing so causes the schema crate to own
  runtime HTTP clients. The Provider Absorption Agent must document the confirmed target module in
  `handoff-provider-absorption.md` with explicit layer rationale before moving any files.
- Review checklist (T-80) must confirm all four layer-boundary conditions: no adapter owns
  selection; no orchestration layer owns wire formats; no contract layer owns HTTP clients; no
  adapter reads `/dev/shm` or D-Bus live state.

---

## REQ-10 — Handoff artifacts produced per agent

**WHEN** each agent completes its phase,
**THEN** it MUST deposit a handoff file in
`.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/` per the contract in spec.md §8.

Acceptance criteria:
- All eight handoff files exist and are non-empty at final acceptance.
- Each handoff records: scope, files changed, contract changes, verification
  commands run, known risks, next-agent dependencies.
